articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino to Man Utd: What does a Pochettino team look like and how will he set up struggling Red Devils?
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino takes over from Michael Carrick at Man Utd; former Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea boss brings Premier League experience to the job but what do his previous roles tell us about how his team might shape up at Old Trafford?
articles.body:
The 54-year-old, who led the United States to the last 16 of the World Cup in his most recent role, is returning to England after previous spells in charge of Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea.

Starting with his Southampton tenure, and including his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain head coach, we look at how he has set his team up in each role - and ponder what he might do at United.

A 4-2-3-1 formation quickly became established as Pochettino's favoured choice at Southampton, where he maintained a similar shape to his predecessor Nigel Adkins but with a dramatically different playing style emphasising pressing high up the pitch.

In terms of personnel, his line-up stayed largely consistent, with Dejan Lovren and Victor Wanyama the only major signings to become starters during his season-and-a-half long spell in charge.

Instead, Pochettino showed his ability to improve the players he already had, with Adam Lallana, Morgan Schneiderlin, Jay Rodriguez, Luke Shaw and Nathanial Clyne among those who flourished - albeit once they had adapted to Pochettino's demands.

"When I started at Southampton, I very much played off the left, No 10; almost a luxury-type player," reflected Lallana later in his career. "When Pochettino came in, it was very apparent from day one there would be no luxury player in his team."

Pochettino adopted the same approach at Spurs, where his side, like his Southampton side, soon became identifiable by their aggression and intensity out of possession, as well as quick, vertical passes to facilitate fast-paced attacks in the style of Marcelo Bielsa.

Pochettino counts former Leeds boss Bielsa as his biggest coaching influence along with Sir Alex Ferguson.

Again, Pochettino predominantly used a 4-2-3-1 formation at Spurs. And again, he helped a large contingent of young players flourish, including Dele Alli and Harry Kane, who combined to devastating effect as Pochettino's No 10 and and No 9 respectively.

Pochettino used his full-backs to provide attacking width, with a central midfielder, usually Eric Dier, encouraged to drop back and form a back three in possession. This in turn allowed Alli, Christian Eriksen and Heung-Min Son to play in close proximity to Kane.

Pochettino used those young players to transform Spurs, reaching a Champions League final and achieving three consecutive top-three Premier League finishes. But the age profile of the team changed as time wore on.

As the team got older, legs became heavier, and adequate replacements failed to arrive from the transfer market, Spurs struggled to sustain their intensity. Pochettino's departure in 2019, five years after his appointment, confirmed the end of a cycle.

Pochettino returned to management over a year after leaving Spurs when took over at Paris-Saint Germain, where his tenure was a story of adapting his philosophy to the characteristics of his players.

To accommodate Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar, Pochettino moved away from the high-pressing tactics that had defined his earlier roles, knowing his superstar front three were not predisposed to such a demanding off-the-ball approach.

A 4-3-3 formation was his most used system, again with attacking full-backs in Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes. But the circumstances meant his PSG side were far removed from his favoured style.

Pochettino used a 3-4-2-1 formation in some of his early games in charge of Chelsea following his appointment in 2023. Soon, though, he switched to his favoured 4-2-3-1.

Cole Palmer followed in the footsteps of previous attackers to have flourished under Pochettino, such as Alli and Kane, with 22 goals and 11 assists in a stunning Premier League campaign.

But overall Pochettino found it difficult to transmit his ideas.

In April of his only season at Stamford Bridge, he questioned the group's mentality and work-rate. "We still need to create this mentality that is going to help us," he said. "You need to demand more from yourself and your team-mates."

Pochettino's Spurs side consistently ranked among the Premier League's top sides in terms of distance covered but Chelsea finished the 2023/24 season with the third-lowest total in the division.

Pochettino continued to adapt with the USA national team, switching between a back three and back four and moving away from the more rigid positional game implemented earlier in his career.

His most used formation at the World Cup was a 4-3-3 but his attacking players were encouraged to be fluid and rotate positions, an approach which helped them overpower Paraguay, Australia and Bosnia and Herzegovina before their elimination by Belgium.

Pochettino was also commended for getting the team to pull together as a collective, with co-ordinated pressing high up the pitch becoming central to their approach at the World Cup, where their average of eight high turnovers per game was among the highest in the competition.

Pochettino's team at Manchester United is likely to look similar, at least initially, to that of Carrick, who also favoured a 4-2-3-1 formation - albeit with a few potential adjustments.

Leny Yoro's recovery speed could be needed at centre-back if he is to play a high line, while the athleticism of Patrick Dorgu could be preferable to the experience of a 31-year-old Shaw. Carlos Baleba is likely to be key in midfield given his physical prowess.

But Pochettino may also have to accept, as in some of his previous roles, that he can't demand a ferociously high-intensity approach given the players he will have at his disposal.

The Argentine typically favours young players but United have one of the oldest starting line-ups in the Premier League this season. Could Shea Lacey provide an injection of youthful energy?

Bruno Fernandes will doubtless be vital in the No 10 role but does he have the energy, at 32, to run beyond his striker in the style of a young Alli with Kane at Spurs?

Can a team that ranks 19th in the division for distance covered this season achieve the level of intensity Pochettino craves?

In possession, Pochettino may seek to develop United's threat from direct attacks and counters, in the style of his Spurs and Chelsea sides. But he will have his work cut out to transform their pressing.

It adds to the intrigue about what might lie ahead. Pochettino feels he has evolved. "If you don't change, you die," he said recently. That attitude will likely be needed at United, where he inherits a very different squad from the one he had in his best years at Spurs.

articles.title: Gary Neville: Mauricio Pochettino needs control of Manchester United recruitment
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Gary Neville says new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino must take control of recruitment to turn things around at Old Trafford; Pochettino has replaced Michael Carrick as head coach
articles.body:
Pochettino has been appointed as successor to the sacked Michael Carrick and will take over with United in the Premier League relegation zone after making their worst-ever start to the competition after 10 games.

Neville is a long-term admirer of Pochettino but says the Argentine will need to oversee a substantial overhaul of the club's squad if he is to significantly improve United's fortunes.

"I'm hoping Mauricio Pochettino has done a couple of things on the way in and I'm hoping he protects himself on his contract because he'll need to," Neville told Sky Sports News.

"I'm sure he's stated that he needs a massive budget. I think he needs defenders straight away to get Manchester United anywhere near where they want to be this season.

"And the other thing is to make sure that he takes control of the recruitment because it's quite clear that what happened in the summer is well below the standard again.

"He's got to come in here and protect himself against actually the people that he's working with. They are currently trying to employ him.

"He needs to make sure he takes the club into his own hands, into his own destiny, make sure he controls his own outcomes and make sure he's absolutely unequivocal in getting money to improve the defence initially in January and improving the midfield and forward line next summer."

For Neville, United need a complete defensive overhaul, further midfield reinforcements and a new centre-forward, with only Kobbie Mainoo currently convincing him in midfield, in a reflection of the rebuild that the incoming boss faces.

He estimates that Pochettino could need around 10 new players to get United back to where they want to be.

"If I said that the midfield that I've seen this season, only Kobbie Mainoo to me looks like he's good enough," said Neville.

"The back line, I think it needs a complete rebuild and I think we need a centre-forward.

"So I don't know how many that is and probably you could argue we need back-up in goal as well.

"So my view would be probably, I don't know yet, there's probably five or six in defence, there's two or three in midfield, there's a goalkeeper and there's probably a centre-forward.

"And I think you're probably looking at about 10 players that you would need to basically rotate out.

"Lisandro Martinez told us that basically the sporting director should have brought more players in the summer, so the players know it themselves.

"So Mauricio Pochettino, who's been around the block and knows how to manage football clubs, he'll have a pretty good idea, having watched Manchester United many times over many years.

Pochettino has been considered for the United job on previous occasions, but Neville has warned him against believing that a change of manager alone will solve the club's problems.

Neville remembers visiting Pochettino at Tottenham during his early days in charge, when the Argentine was already identifying which players he wanted to build around and which he needed to move on.

"I think the mistake that Mauricio could make if he comes in is that he may get an initial bounce out of them. He may get six months of bounce out of them," Neville continued.

"I actually remember going to see him at Tottenham in his very early days. We used to, when I was coaching with England, train at Tottenham's training ground.

"He set out very quickly within the first six to eight months in the job. He had a whiteboard in front of him in his office with all the players' names on little markers and he actually moved a group of players over to the left-hand side of the board and said: 'These are the ones I know I need to get rid of. These are the ones I know I can work with and build around.'

"He's got to identify that very quickly at United and I'm sure he will do that. He's more experienced now than he was when he was at Tottenham.

"But he's got a big job to do in exiting players. Manchester United have been really poor at exiting players over the last 10 years. They've not done it very well at all."

Neville's admiration for Pochettino - but is he the right appointment?

Neville has made no secret of his admiration for Pochettino and believes the Argentine has the coaching ability and personality to manage a club of United's stature.

But he has also seen too many different types of manager fail at Old Trafford to believe the challenge will be straightforward.

David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick have all experienced the difficulties of the job, while Ralf Rangnick also failed to turn things around.

For Neville, that history should serve as a warning to Pochettino.

"I can't believe Mauricio would have looked at the last 13 years, looked at managers like David Moyes, Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal who are very experienced, brilliant operators in what they do and seen them fall short.

"He's then seen talented managers from Europe like Amorim and Ten Hag fall short.

"He's seen club legends who have got a lot of love for the club, who understand the values, understand how to play for Manchester United, understand what the fans want and can communicate that. He's seen those guys fail.

"He's seen Ralf Rangnick come in, who's got more of a sporting director background and a business background, come in and fail and tell the club they need open-heart surgery.

"So he's seen every type of manager fail at this football club over the last 13 years.

"He's got to come in and basically wipe the slate clean and start from scratch and imagine that this football club is a blank canvas because everybody that's been there in that period has been part of the failure."

Despite those concerns, Neville has consistently backed Pochettino as a candidate for the job and believes he has the qualities to succeed.

"I've always wanted Mauricio Pochettino as the manager at United. I've said it numerous times that I wanted him.

"I think he's a brilliant person. I think he'll handle the media. I think he understands the size of the club.

"But it's a monumental task to win everybody else over and get everybody on side and make sure he has a team that can compete.

"He's a brilliant coach with great experience and he's a good man.

"He also believes in young players and bringing players through and developing them and coaching them, which is what he's going to have to do at Manchester United.

"I've always liked Mauricio Pochettino. Whether this is the right point for him to take the Manchester United job, who knows? We'll find out in the next year or two.

"But I'm hoping that he's made some pretty strong demands on the way in and that he's got control of the club."

articles.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Sleepers: Puka Nacua injury opens up opportunity for Konata Mumpfield
articles.summary: Scott Pianowski shares some underrated fantasy football options for your lineup off the waiver wire for Week 10.
articles.body:
DeMario Douglas was the lone hit on the sleeper page last week , while Adonai Mitchell drove us batty (seven targets, tons of air yards, no catches). We're onto Week 10. Let's see what undervalued options we can find.

RB Audric Estimé vs. Panthers (36%) : The status of this sleeper comes down to Travis Etienne Jr.'s health — if Etienne is ready to play again, Estimé is too risky to use. But Estimé came out of nowhere to post a useful 15-72-1 log last week, and the Panthers have been the second-easiest defense for RBs to score against.

WR Konata Mumpfield at Cardinals (12%) : He's had just one relevant game all year, a 4-93-1 surprise at the Broncos in Week 3. But with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both hurt, the Rams need some new songs in the passing game; perhaps this is a reasonable spot for Mumpfield and Sons. The Cardinals have been an average matchup for pass production.

RB Dylan Sampson vs. Texans (28%) : The Houston defense is parceling out just 3.9 YPC, so it could be another slog for RB Quinshon Judkins. So we'll leave the light on for Sampson, who has 12 catches the last three weeks and is coming off a season-best 11 touches. Deshaun Watson is also returning, and he steered six passes to Sampson two weeks ago.

QB Aaron Rodgers at Bengals (42%) : Hopefully you don't need a QB streamer this week, though Caleb Williams managers might in a pinch. Rodgers has seen his fantasy score drop in his last three games, but he's rested off the bye and facing a Cincinnati team that could be weary after a Europe trip. Rodgers posted 23 fantasy points when the teams met in Week 3.

RB Kaleb Johnson vs. Vikings (16%) : It's probably a touchdown-or-bust case for Johnson, as the Minnesota defense has been outstanding all year. But solving for volume is most of the puzzle when scouting RBs, and Johnson might be the last back standing in Green Bay, with Josh Jacobs (finger) out and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain. Johnson was surprisingly useful (14-68-1) at New England last week.

WR Jordan Watkins at Cowboys (5%) : Do your injury diligence on this one, as the Niners aren't sure if Mike Evans or Deebo Samuel Sr. will play this week. If even one of them sits at Dallas, then Watkins could be in play against one of the league's worst defenses. Watkins had an impressive 4-86-1 breakout against the Raiders last week, including a nifty TD catch on a contested target.

TE Darren Waller at Saints (18%) : Maybe you shrugged off his Week 9 breakout, as the Broncos are a TE-funnel defense. But the Saints are the seventh-friendliest defense for TE production, so Waller can help us again. His target share seems to fluctuate weekly, but he always offers touchdown equity (four spikes in eight starts), and that's what tight-end streaming is usually about.

articles.title: España-Inglaterra, el mejor fútbol del mundo
articles.standfirst: La campeona del mundo contra la tercera clasificada, dos escuelas dominantes, Bellingham frente al mejor centro del campo, Kane y Lamine, la cantera, las finales femeninas...
articles.summary: La campeona del mundo contra la tercera clasificada, dos escuelas dominantes, Bellingham frente al mejor centro del campo, Kane y Lamine, la cantera, las finales femeninas...
articles.body: España e Inglaterra se enfrentan en el Metropolitano para disputarse la primera plaza del grupo de la Nations League, pero también para hacer chocar a los modelos más dominantes del fútbol mundial. Frente a frente estarán las dos mejores escuelas del mundo, los dos modelos de formación que más talento producen, las dos selecciones que han convertido la excelencia en una costumbre y las dos referencias sobre las que gira el fútbol internacional desde hace varios años. Una rivalidad de altura. Durante décadas, ambos países compartieron una paradoja similar. Y miserias. Dos naciones históricas, dos potencias futbolísticas, dos ligas influyentes y dos canteras inagotables que, sin embargo, vivían muy por debajo de sus posibilidades cuando llegaba la hora de levantar trofeos. Inglaterra suma décadas aferrada al recuerdo del Mundial 1966, su única corona. España cargó durante generaciones con la etiqueta de selección brillante pero incapaz de trasladar su talento a los grandes campeonatos. Dos gigantes que producían admiración, pero no títulos. La diferencia es que España logró romper definitivamente esa barrera. Lo hizo primero con la generación que conquistó dos Eurocopas y un Mundial entre 2008 y 2012, y lo ha vuelto a hacer con una nueva hornada que ya suma Nations League, Eurocopa y Mundia. Lo que parecía una excepción se ha convertiuod en una cultura ganadora. Mientras Inglaterra sigue buscando el gran título que confirme el potencial de una generación extraordinaria, España se ha transformado en la selección más victoriosa del siglo XXI entre las grandes potencias europeas, un equipo capaz de reinventarse sin perder el hábito de competir por todo. El partido del domingo es, en cierto modo, el enfrentamiento entre dos caminos que parten de un origen parecido pero que han desembocado en realidades distintas. Inglaterra ha conseguido construir una de las canteras más impresionantes del planeta. La revolución impulsada durante la última década ha producido futbolistas de primer nivel en prácticamente todas las posiciones. España, por su parte, no solo ha mantenido intacta su capacidad formativa, sino que ha conseguido algo todavía más difícil: enlazar generaciones ganadoras. Cuando desaparecieron los Xavi, Iniesta, Busquets, Ramos, Villa, Torres..., parecía inevitable una transición larga. Sin embargo, el relevo ya está aquí. Esa la grandeza del duelo del Metropolitano. No es solo la campeona del mundo contra la tercera clasificada del planeta. No es únicamente la finalista y la campeona de la última Eurocopa. Es el choque entre las dos fábricas de talento más admiradas del momento. Entre dos selecciones que dominan también las categorías inferiores y que llevan años encontrándose en los escenarios más importantes. La final de la última Eurocopa absoluta. La final del Europeo sub 21 de hace dos ediciones. La de Mundial sub 17 de 2017. Numerosos enfrentamientos decisivos en torneos juveniles. Una rivalidad que se ha ido construyendo generación tras generación y que ya forma parte del paisaje habitual del fútbol internacional. La competencia se extiende incluso más allá del fútbol masculino. Inglaterra derrotó a España en la final de la Eurocopa femenina de 2025. Un año antes, España golpeó más fuerte conquistando el Mundial en Australia ante las inglesas. Cuando dos países coinciden en la cima tanto en categoría masculina como femenina, en las absolutas y en las inferiores, ya no se trata de una buena generación. Se trata de una estructura de excelencia. Y sobre ese contexto colectivo aparecen las figuras que convierten un gran partido en un acontecimiento mundial. Jude Bellingham simboliza al futbolista total, dominante física y técnicamente, capaz de decidir encuentros desde cualquier zona del campo. "El mejor centrocampista que hay hoy en el mundo", asegura Mourinho. Del otro lado emerge el que muchos consideran el mejor centro del campo del mundo como unidad competitiva, una colección de futbolistas que mantienen vigente la gran tradición española de gobernar los partidos a través del balón, a través de Fabián, Pedri, Merino, Zubimendi, los ahora Rodri y Olmo, el futuro con Barrios... "Tenemos a los mejores centrocampistas del mundo", sostien De la Fuente. También estarán frente a frente dos de las imágenes más poderosas del fútbol actual. Harry Kane, Balón de Oro y uno de los delanteros más completos de su generación, representa la madurez competitiva de Inglaterra. Lamine Yamal, que fue bronce, encarna el futuro, aunque cada vez resulte más difícil seguir llamándolo así. Con apenas unos años en la élite, ya se ha instalado entre los nombres que aspiran a marcar una época y entre los candidatos naturales a los grandes premios individuales durante la próxima década. Lamine, con 19 años, es campeón de Europa y del Mundo. Le falta la Nations. Kane, con 33, busca ser el capitán que acabe con una maldición de 60 años y que a él le ha hecho ya perder dos finales de Eurocopa y dos semifinales de Mundiales tras ir ganado en las dos. Por todo eso el Metropolitano albergará mucho más que un partido de Nations League. Será una fotografía perfecta del fútbol actual. Las dos mejores escuelas del mundo. Dos países que llevan años disputándose finales, títulos y generaciones. Dos modelos que producen talento como nadie. Y, sobre todo, una rivalidad cada vez más profunda entre una Inglaterra que sigue buscando el trofeo que confirme todo lo que promete y una España que ya convirtió aquella vieja frustración histórica en una costumbre ganadora. Si el siglo XXI ha tenido una selección capaz de transformar el talento en hegemonía, esa ha sido España. Y el domingo vuelve a enfrentarse al único rival que parece preparado para discutirle el relevo.

articles.title: Oihan Sancet, del "sueño" de defender a España al "sueño" de jugar con Euskadi un Mundial
articles.standfirst: El navarro Oihan Sancet fue convocado por primera vez con España en 2023 y acaba de ser convocado por la seleccion de Euskadi
articles.summary: El navarro Oihan Sancet fue convocado por primera vez con España en 2023 y acaba de ser convocado por la seleccion de Euskadi
articles.body: Oihan Sancet, mediapunta del Athletic Club, debutó con la selección absoluta de España el 12 de octubre de 2023 en un partido ante Escocia de la fase de clasificación para la Eurocopa 2024. España ganó 2-0 y el mediapunta de Pamplona, que entró al terreno de juego en el minuto 67 sustituyendo a Mikel Merino, marcó el 2-0 en el minuto 86. "Estoy muy contento con el debut y contento con los tres puntos", declaró Sancet en Estadio de La Cartuja (Sevilla) en Teledeporte. Sancet reconoció "que no me esperaba el salto desde la sub-21. Me dedicaba a trabajar bien en mi equipo y hacerlo lo mejor posible. El momento ha llegado y estoy muy feliz". Tras su primera convocatoria con España Oihan Sancet, que escogió el dorsal 7 y que ha sido cuatro veces internacional absoluto, confesó que "estoy muy contento el poder estar aquí... y es un sueño, la verdad". "Recibí un mensaje de mi padre diciendo que estaba convocado, y lo primero que hago es llamar a mi madre para contarle que estoy en la selección. Estamos muy contentos", compartió. Oihan Sancet, tras su reciente primera convocatoria con la selección de Euskadi, ha declarado que "ojalá algún día podamos pelear un Mundial con la selección de nuestro país". El mediapunta navarro confesó que vestir la camiseta del combinado vasco es "un orgullo y lo que sueñas desde pequeño, jugar con la selección que amas". "Ojalá el día de mañana pueda ser oficial y nos podamos medir en un Mundial contra los más grandes. Es el objetivo principal que tenemos que conseguir entre todos, poco a poco. Sabemos que es difícil, pero poniendo cada uno su granito de arena creo que puede llegar algún día. Lo que digo, un orgullo y soñar el día de mañana estar jugando contra los mejores... Ojalá el día de mañana podamos pelear un Mundial con la selección de nuestro país", explicó.

articles.title: Caída de Outlook y Teams a nivel mundial: fallos en el sistema Microsoft 365 durante horas
articles.standfirst: No funciona en todo el mundo el correo, teams, sharepoint…
articles.summary: No funciona en todo el mundo el correo, teams, sharepoint…
articles.body: Siguen los problemas. En este caso a afecta a la tecnología pero a nivel mundial después de que se haya producido una caída de Microsoft 365 que comenzó este jueves y ya ha afectado a usuarios de Outlook y a varias herramientas de la compañía. De hecho, Microsoft ha confirmado que el fallo en Exchange Online, su servicio de correo en la nube, puede impedir que algunos usuarios abran su buzón tanto en la web como en la aplicación de escritorio y causar retrasos en la entrega de mensajes. Desde anoche se está estudiando el escenario... y el vicepresidente ejecutivo de Copilot en Microsoft, Charles Lamanna, ha descartado que sea por un ataque cibernético. La empresa, por su parte, intenta recuperar este viernes la normalidad en sus operaciones. "Por ahora, puedo confirmar que no hay indicios de que esto sea el resultado de una actividad maliciosa o cibernética", escribió en X Lamanna. Estas incomodidades han afectado a servicios como el gestor de correo electrónico Outlook y la plataforma de videoconferencias Teams "en cualquier región". Según explicó la propia compañía en X, una parte de la infraestructura en "múltiples regiones" ha experimentado una "carga elevada", que se ha traducido en errores de conectividad.

articles.title: Zidane no recula tras su primera derrota con Francia y se encomienda a Mbappé
articles.standfirst: "El resultado no cambia nada en absoluto"
articles.summary: "El resultado no cambia nada en absoluto"
articles.body: Zinedine Zidane, seleccionador Francia, lamentó la segunda parte de su equipo en Italia (1-3) en la que supone su primera derrota al frente de los 'Bleus'. El exjugador del Real Madrid dejó claro que, a pesar de la derrota, no tiene intención de cambiar sus principios de juego. "Empezamos muy bien; tuvimos la posesión y creamos ocasiones. Después, pasamos apuros en la segunda parte, sobre todo en defensa; esa es mi explicación...", declaró el técnico galo en rueda de prensa. Zidane subrayó que "no nos faltó valentía; al contrario, estábamos metidos en el partido. Pero, en defensa, estuvimos menos acertados. Sin el balón, no fue suficiente; nos desmoronamos tras el descanso y nos salimos de nuestro planteamiento, pero todo esto forma parte de nuestro aprendizaje. Lo analizaremos. Ahora nos centraremos en la recuperación. Son aspectos en los que debemos trabajar: todos defendimos peor, pero seguiremos fieles a nuestros principios de juego". "Habrá que ganar el próximo partido (contra Turquía); sin duda, vamos a descansar para prepararnos bien, pero, pase lo que pase, había que ganar este último encuentro. ¿Habrá cambios en Burdeos? Sí, está previsto hacer cambios; el partido de esta noche contra Italia y su resultado no cambian nada en absoluto", insistió. Zinedine Zidane reconoció que "quedamos os un poco decepcionados con nuestra proporción de ocasiones durante la primera concentración en relación con nuestra posesión; esta vez generamos ocasiones claras, así que ha mejorado, pero nos ha faltado eficacia. Hubo dos balones al poste, así son las cosas... Tuvimos las situaciones. Lo que analizo es que no estuvimos lo suficientemente bien sin el balón. Debemos corregirlo para el próximo partido". Preguntado por el estado de Mbappé el seleccionador de Francia dejó claro que Mbappé podrá estar el domingo contra Turquía. "¿Si Hay alguna posibilidad de ver a Mbappé el domingo? ¡Espero que incluso dos! (Risas). Estaba previsto que descansara hoy (contra Italia) y jugara el domingo (contra Turquía. Así que espero que juegue, sí", confirmó.

articles.title: Scotland v North Macedonia: How big a problem is central defence for Sebastien Pocognoli?
articles.summary: Amy Canavan assesses Scotland's central defensive dilemmas before Friday evening's must-win match against North Macedonia.
articles.body:
On Andy Robertson's night, it's difficult to not peek across the rest of the Scotland defensive line and worry.

The left-back will be lauded - whether he likes it or not - as he earns his 102nd cap, equalling Kenny Dalglish's men's record, against North Macedonia on Friday.

The captain is calling for it to be the King's night as much as his, and while the pair of Liverpool greats can have - and laugh - that out between them, the grace period for a giggle for Sebastien Pocognoli is petering out.

After an underwhelming opening camp, the head coach is in desperate need of a first home win - which he is hoping will come against the only side he's been victorious against in his opening four games.

The starting back three from that night in Skopje - Stephen Welsh, Scott McKenna and Luis Binks - are all out injured, forcing the Belgian to dig deep into the pool of central defenders, where he has pulled out a pair of names from the past in an attempt to arrest the porousness that plagued his debut international window.

Forgotten men Ryan Porteous and David Bates - the latter who last played international football seven years ago - join established but recent red card receiver Jack Hendry, and handful-of Scotland-minutes man Luke Graham as the centre-back quartet - but how much of a problem area is it already proving to be for Pocognoli?

Nations League: Scotland v North Macedonia

In comparison to the embarrassment of riches the head coach has in midfield and, more sparingly, in the forward areas, the heart of the back line is a bit bare.

Whoever slots alongside Tottenham Hotspur's Robertson - whether in Pocognoli's preferred back three, which could see Kieran Tierney shift in on the left side, or flat four - it's unlikely the combined caps haul of his centre-back buddies will come nearly close to his century plus.

The last of Los Angeles FC’s Porteous' 13 came against Greece in March 2025, while Bates picked up four under Alex McLeish six years before that.

Saudi Arabia-based Hendry is closing in on the half-century, while Celtic’s Tierney has surpassed it. Graham got a matter of minutes in North Macedonia after McKenna was dismissed.

Bates was playing in Germany with Hamburg when he faced Albania, Israel, Kazakhstan and San Marino and, after stints at a couple of clubs in Belgium, he's found himself with newly promoted albeit impressive Turkish Super Lig side Amedspor.

"There are a lot of players who are not available for the defensive line, but [David's] not there for nothing," Pocognoli said at Hampden Park on Thursday.

"He's there because he's performing well in Turkey with a team third in the rankings, in a tough competition."

Managed by Besnik Hasi - who played and managed in the Belgian's homeland - the head coach added: "I know the coach there as well, so I know he's also demanding a lot to the players.

"I can imagine the spirit in which he trains every day and I think for this camp, his experience can help some aspects on the pitch."

No excuses as Pocognoli seeks first Hampden victory

Robertson set to make history but his hero Dalglish will always be King

Dalkeith to LA pays off for Porteous with Scotland recall

Surely with no-one more so than Stoke City defender Graham, who has been tipped for a start by former England international Kevin Phillips.

Dundee's star performer last season has thrived for the Championship club this term - on the left of a back three - leaving many members of the Tartan Army deflated by the lack of minutes he was afforded last time out.

He came on after 88 minutes in the North Macedonian capital.

They might not be the only ones, too, given the in-form 22-year-old is now, surely, in pole position to face an under-firing North Macedonian front-line.

Friday's visitors have gone 12 games without a victory, failing to score in the latest eight and have lost their past five while conceding 14 goals.

They were "unlucky" to see the Swiss score three though, in Pocognoli's view. How he would take that scoreline in his side's favour now.

Victory is a near-must on matchday five. Sound and solid tactics, with a flavour of imagination and invention too wouldn't go amiss.

The latter qualities were seen as shortcomings of his predecessor, Steve Clarke, but stability in defence was a trademark of Clarke's tenure.

It's imperative Pocognoli picks up that mantle in his search for his first win at Hampden.

articles.title: Raphinha, muy emocionado: "Quiero estar disponible no solo para la selección, también para el Barça"
articles.standfirst: El extremo se defiende, en su rueda de prensa con Brasil, de las duras críticas recibidas
articles.summary: El extremo se defiende, en su rueda de prensa con Brasil, de las duras críticas recibidas
articles.body: Raphinha atendió hoy a los medios de comunicación, junto a Carlo Ancelotti, en la previa del encuentro de Brasil contra Japón que se disputa mañana sábado en Singapur. El extremo culé se emocionó a la hora de defenderse de las duras criticas recibidas por sus palabras sobre la dosificación que necesita tener con la Canarinha para no caer, nuevamente, lesionado. En su renovación con el Barcelona, hasta 2030, Raphinha aseveró que contactó con el extécnico del Real Madrid para minimizar el riesgo de sufrir dolencias a causa de la carga de partidos. "Sabe que tiene que gestionar mis minutos y que una lesión haría que llegara peor a un próximo parón. He hablado con él, estoy muy bien, pero aún no estoy al cien por cien. Intento hacer todo lo posible para estar lo mejor posible físicamente", dijo el internacional brasileño. Estas palabras le comportaron grandes y duras críticas en su país, que en su comparecencia de hoy quiso explicar. "En aquel momento, cuando me hicieron la pregunta y respondí, creí que estaba siendo claro en lo que quería decir; al menos en mi cabeza me pareció que lo era. Teniendo en cuenta todo lo que he pasado en las últimas tres convocatorias, con tres lesiones prácticamente en la misma zona de la pierna, lo que quise decir fue, simplemente, que tenía que cuidarme. Evidentemente, no quiero volver a lesionarme. Quiero estar disponible no solo para la selección, sino también para el Barcelona", comentó Raphinha, visiblemente emocionado y contrariado porque se puso en duda su implicación con su bloque nacional. El capitán barcelonista reconoció lo mucho que le habían afectado los comentarios negativos recibidos, hasta el punto de ponerse en duda su profesionalidad y compromiso con la Canarinha: "Es natural que una crítica nos afecte. Somos seres humanos y, por mucho que lo intentemos, algunas cosas nos afectan. Es natural. Cualquiera en mi lugar, recibiendo críticas sabiendo que lo está dando todo, estaría afectado. Tenemos que estar preparados para las críticas, defender Brasil es algo muy grande". Raphinha destacó que será el primero en dar un paso al lado si ve que no puede aportar lo suficiente al equipo. "Por desgracia, cuando no estamos bien físicamente no podemos jugar ni aquí ni en el club. También dije que, si mi cuerpo me lo permite, siempre daré lo mejor de mí. Cuando vea que físicamente no puedo rendir, seré el primero en retirarme, porque soy muy autocrítico conmigo mismo. Sí, lo que dije tuvo una mala repercusión, aunque en su momento pensé que lo había explicado bien. Pero forma parte del juego por desgracia", añadió el exprofesional del Leeds, Pichichi de LaLiga con 15 goles. Raphinha recordó, además, lo que sufrió con su lesión durante el Mundial y las implicaciones que tuvo. "Particularmente fue muy frustrante. Era un momento relevante en mi vida, era importante para la selección y no me notaba al cien por cien físicamente. Solo jugué dos partidos con el Barça tras la lesión contra Francia en el parón previo a la Copa del Mundo. Cuando estás dentro del campo no piensas en las molestias, quieres dar lo mejor de ti. Siempre doy el cien por cien. Muchas veces los médicos y los fisioterapeutas me piden calma, pero no puedo cambiar mi estilo de juego. Pero el cuerpo lo cobra y necesita tiempo para recuperarse. Fue frustrante", aseveró, reflexivo, el goleador azulgrana. El capitán culé insistió en su firme compromiso con la Canarinha: "Desde la primera vez que me puse la camiseta de la selección siempre dejé muy clara mi voluntad de estar aquí. Nunca renuncié a la selección brasileña y siempre hice todo lo posible por estar presente. A veces, no he podido venir, pero siempre he hecho todo lo que estaba en mi mano para poder estar aquí y vestir la camiseta de la Seleçao. Para mí, siempre ha sido un honor y un privilegio, y siempre lo será. Eso no va a cambiar, independientemente del tiempo que esté aquí".

articles.title: Cole Palmer: 'It's a lie' Chelsea forward does not want to play for England, says team-mate Morgan Rogers
articles.summary: Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer was not part of Thomas Tuchel's squad for England's Nations League double header this month with Croatia and Spain; Palmer withdrew from September's internationals with injury; club-mate Morgan Rogers says it is a "lie" Palmer doesn't want to play for England
articles.body:
The Chelsea playmaker, who did not make last summer's World Cup squad, was not called up by England manager Thomas Tuchel for the Uefa Nations League double header with Croatia, which the Three Lions won 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday, and in Spain on Sunday night.

The German made headlines in September when he said Palmer, 24, "misses too many opportunities to impress him" following the attacker's withdrawal from that month's Nations League fixtures due to injury.

However, Rogers - who opened the scoring against Croatia - has rushed to Palmer's defence.

"It's a lie," Rogers told BBC Radio 5 Live of his Chelsea team-mate, who has contributed five goals and three assists in 12 games in all competitions this season.

"He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

"We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he's been managing them injuries ever since. He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100 per cent himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself.

"Of course he does, who wouldn't? But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10/15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it. It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England.

"You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it. But it's something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country."

However, when asked about the quotes in his post-match press conference after England beat Croatia, Tuchel said: "It's totally fine. He's his team-mate and friend, so why wouldn't he?

"I was very happy with the commitment of Morgan Rogers and that's what matters."

Tuchel sends out clear message with Palmer decision

"In leaving Cole Palmer out of this squad, Thomas Tuchel has sent a clear message to both the Chelsea man, and to every other England wannabe, whatever your status and experience in international football.

"The message is stark - you have to be present, you have to be committed, you have to be humble, as part of a wider push for a positive squad dynamic. And for Tuchel, it is clear he feels Palmer has not done enough to prove he has those three qualities. Tuchel doesn't doubt his ability - eight goal involvements in 11 matches is a much better output than either Ebe Eze or Morgan Gibbs-White have managed so far this season. And yet they are both in, and Palmer is out.

"When he withdrew from the last England squad in September because of a minor injury, that was the final straw for Tuchel. Five times, since the German coach took over in January 2025, Palmer has been unavailable because of injury. On two of those occasions, Tuchel named Palmer in his squad, only for him to withdraw. He has only played three matches in the Tuchel era.

"If he had picked Palmer this time, and dropped another number 10 to accommodate him, that would have been entirely the wrong message that Tuchel wanted to portray to the rest of his squad.

"Tuchel expects the sort of loyalty and determination shown by John Stones, Jude Bellingham and - most recently - Declan Rice, who have all chosen to still spend some time with the squad, even when they weren't fit enough to play.

"So, the England boss has made an example of the man who scored for his country in a Euros final two years ago. And that should be taken as a warning to Palmer personally, and as a cautionary tale to everyone else who wants to be part of his England squad."

articles.title: David Beckham to be inducted into US National Soccer Hall of Fame in 2027
articles.summary: Former England captain David Beckham is set to be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class.
articles.body:
David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class.

The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract.

He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield.

Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023.

His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas.

He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey".

Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time."

Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility.

Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019.

"To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram.

articles.title: England Wheelchair crowned Rugby League World Cup champions with victory over France
articles.summary: England are back-to-back Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup champions with victory over France in Australia; There has been five Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup finals with England and France contesting all five; England have now won three
articles.body:
It means England are the back-to-back world champions following their 2022 victory on home soil.

Of the five Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup finals that have taken place, England have now won three, with France winning it in 2013 and 2017.

The Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup final was brilliantly poised at 28-22 to England at half-time after a quick start and impressive end to the first 40 that saw Joe Coyd claim his hat-trick and Rob Hawkins and Jack Brown go over.

A strong middle spell from France meant they added four tries through Jeremy Bourson, Leo Hivernat, Damien Dore, and Florian Guttadoro but had a six-point deficit to make up.

While Dany Denuwelaere went over for a second half hat-trick for France, a fourth try for Coyd, Hawkins' second, and two more for Brown cemented England as the three-time champions of the world.

Just five minutes into the first half, it was Coyd who went over and sliced through twice in quick succession, once from close range and then once a brilliant break through as England got off to an impressive start for a 10-0 lead.

Despite England's fast start, it did not take long for France to hit back after a penalty. They sent the ball out wide for Bourson to go over in the corner. With the conversion, they trailed by just four points.

France then struck again after a brilliant pass gave Hivernat the space out wide to race away and score after 20 minutes of play. The conversion was missed and scores were level at 10-10.

The momentum was all with France and they made it count through their backline. Off the back of another penalty, this time given away by Coyd, they went out to Dore who had the space to score. They were then too quick once again on the right and Guttadoro was in. The conversion from Hivernat had France 16-10 up with 15 minutes remaining in the first half.

While France had been in control for over 20 minutes, Coyd made sure to get England back into the game and get his hat-trick in the process. Nathan Collins converted and it was a six-point game.

The Golden Boot winner Hawkins then created a golden moment with four minutes left on the clock with Brown following up with a contender for the try of the tournament as he went flying over and grounded Hawkins' kick with seconds remaining on the clock. With the conversion, England led 28-22 at half-time.

The frantic nature of the final continued early in the second half as a try from Denuwelaere was met by Hawkins' second to reinstate England's advantage.

The arm wrestle then ensued and with big collisions, and Coyd used exactly that to get his fourth, his massive strength moving the defender out the way. However, Denuwelaere then took his opportunity to show his brute force and with a powerful effort, France trailed by four with just over 15 minutes remaining.

It was truly a game of cat and mouse as, just as Denuwelaere had scored, Brown then came through on a brilliant line which defied the France defence.

France could see the clock ticking and with that, moved away from their game plan and gave away penalties, their frenzied approach handing England the advantage. That saw Brown step up once again and go in for his hat-trick and with Collins' conversion, England led 50-34 with 10 minutes to play.

France battled and tried to chance their arm and did get a consolation through Denuwelaere once again but besides that, England stayed solid defensively to be crowned world champions once again.

Brown: It felt like an out of body experience!

Jack Brown speaking following England's victory and clinching his third World Cup win…

"I am feeling a bit out of body at the moment. It was an incredible display and it was just so much fun playing with the guys.

"We said we had to work hard for each other and that is what we did today.

"There were five minutes left and I looked up and I went 'damn are we that far ahead'.

"Five minutes to go was when I saw the light at the end of the tunnel to slow down the game and control the ending.

articles.title: Gravísima lesión de Alfon: sufre una rotura del cruzado anterior
articles.standfirst: El extremo se dañó en un lance del entrenamiento del jueves
articles.summary: El extremo se dañó en un lance del entrenamiento del jueves
articles.body: Gravísima lesión de Alfon. Según ha comunicado esta mañana el Sevilla en un comunicado, el extremo manchego sufrió una rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla derecha en el entrenamiento del jueves. Alfon fue trasladado de inmediato a un centro médico para que se le practicara una resonancia, que ha confirmado el diagnóstico inicial. Alfon será operado en los próximos días. La lesión de Alfon, que será operado en los próximos días, supone uno de los golpes más duros que puede recibir cualquier futbolista profesional a lo largo de su carrera deportiva. Esta grave dolencia lo mantendrá alejado de los terrenos de juego durante una extensa horquilla de tiempo de entre seis y ocho meses. Si la intervención quirúrgica y los plazos de rehabilitación marchan según lo previsto, el atacante comenzará a reincorporarse en la pretemporada de 2027. La baja de Alfon llega en un momento especialmente delicado y complejo para la demarcación de extremo dentro del Sevilla. Esta nueva ausencia se suma directamente a la reciente lesión de Miguel Sierra, quien tampoco podrá volver a competir hasta el próximo cambio de año. Como consecuencia directa de ambos contratiempos médicos, los carriles del ataque nervionense quedan literalmente cogidos con alfileres para afrontar el calendario. El exjugador del Celta de Vigo había asumido precisamente el rol de sustituto habitual de Félix Correia durante los últimos compromisos oficiales del equipo. A día de hoy, el atacante portugués se erige como el único futbolista totalmente fijo e indiscutible en los planes tácticos de Luis García Plaza.

articles.title: La redención de Grealish: el 'Party Boy' pide "perdón" por su última liada

articles.summary: "Quiero pedir disculpas a los aficionados y a todos en el club por no haber podido ayudar al equipo durante las últimas semanas. Me encanta jugar para este club"
articles.body: Jack Grealish, el 'Party Boy' que Pep Guardiola no pudo reconducir en el Manchester City, ha pedido disculpas a los aficionados del Everton por su reciente ausencia, motivada por "una infracción de la disciplina del club". El centrocampista de 31 años, que está cedido por el Manchester City, se perdió los dos partidos de los 'Toffees' contra el Newcastle United y la victoria frente al Coventry previa al parón de selecciones. Jack Grealish regresó a la actividad participando en una victoria a puerta cerrada contra el Derby County de la Championship. "Es un placer estar de vuelta con el resto del equipo tras unos buenos días de entrenamiento. Quiero pedir disculpas a los aficionados y a todos en el club por no haber podido ayudar al equipo durante las últimas semanas. Me encanta jugar para este club y tengo muchas ganas de volver a jugar ante vosotros vistiendo la camiseta del Everton. Nos vemos pronto", escribió en un mensaje que publicó en Instagram. Grealish busca relanzar su carrera en el Everton, tras haber perdido protagonismo en el Manchester City, a pesar de que su fichaje costó al 'citizen' 118 millones de euros en 2021. Esta temporada Jack Grealish, que está en su último año de contrato con el City por el que cobra 360.000 euros semanales, ha jugado ocho partidos con el Everton. Jack Grealish, el jugador inglés más caro, ha visto lastrada su carrera en el Manchester City por si irregularidad y a su reconocida afición a las fiestas y el alcohol. En abril de 2025 el mediático centrocampista de Birmingham fue cazado dejándose cerca de 6.000 euros en la barra del Bagatelle, famoso club restaurante del West End de Londres, en el que se le vio celebrar con el famoso gesto del Lobo de Wall Street. En 2023 Jack Grealish se convirtió en el gran protagonista de las celebraciones del Manchester City tras ganar Champions, Premier y FA Cup. La mediática juerga alcohólica de Grealish, que durante un fin de semana de locura se trasladó por Ibiza, Turquía y Manchester, se convirtió en noticia en medios de comunicación de medio mundo. "Vivo en un mundo de dolor", llegó a decir Grealish durante "el mejor fin de semana de su vida". En unas palabras que publicó el 'Daily Mail' el futbolista del Manchester City reconoció que "no me arrepiento, ¡así soy cuando estoy de fiesta!". "En realidad, no suelo ser así, pero hemos ganado el triplete y es algo que nunca volverá a suceder. Así que fui y lo disfruté y no fui el único. Creo que muchas veces verás a todos grabándome, pero podría mostrarte cosas en las que otros estaban igual... Nunca me sentaría aquí y te mentiría y diría "No bebo y no salgo de fiesta" porque lo hago. Pero entonces hay tantas personas que vendrán aquí y te dirán "Yo no hago esto, yo no hago aquello" cuando lo hacen. Sólo soy sincero. Estoy viviendo mi sueño de jugar en el mejor club del mundo", reflexionó. En 2023 Jack Grealish fue grabado bailando con una mujer que no era su novia (la modelo Sasha Attwood) mientras le acariciaba la pierna durante una fiesta en Ibiza. La prensa inglesa informó que Sasha Attwood se encontraba de vacaciones en Italia, en la Costa Amalfitana y que la mujer con la que baila Grealish se llamaba Dolly, y era azafata de British Airways. En 2022 Jack Grealish fue cazado en una fiesta piscinera en Las Vegas con unos amigos y junto a una joven morena que no era su novia, Sasha Attwood. Durante la fiesta en la piscina Jack Grealish y sus ocho amigos bebiendo cuatro botellas de tamaño jeroboam (equivalente a dos magnums) de Rock Angel Rosé valoradas en 3.567 euros cada una de ellas. Después de la fiesta un miembro del equipo de seguridad le pidió el teléfono a un grupo de chicas en bikini que estaban en la piscina y que, según el diario 'The Sun', se dirigieron minutos después a las habitaciones de Grealish y sus amigos en el Encore de Las Vegas Strip. Jack Grealish, que disfrutó en Las Vegas de un paquete VIP de 92.993 euros por el que tenía derecho a 116 botellas de champán en un reservado, fue visto en un club nocturno (Zouk) de Las Vegas acompañado de una joven morena.

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel urges England fans to forgive Ben White as Arsenal star faces Wembley boos during Croatia win
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel has urged England supporters to move past their grievances with Ben White after the Arsenal defender was subjected to jeers during the Three Li...
articles.body:
Thomas Tuchel has urged England supporters to move past their grievances with Ben White after the Arsenal defender was subjected to jeers during the Three Lions' latest outing. Despite a winning performance against Croatia, the lingering tension from White's previous international exile remains a talking point at Wembley.

White was introduced as a substitute during England's 2-1 Nations League victory over Croatia on Thursday. The 29-year-old was met with jeers from sections of the home crowd, contrasting sharply with the warm applause afforded to veteran Croatian midfielder Luka Modric.

The hostile reception stems from White's abrupt departure from the 2022 World Cup in Qatar under former manager Gareth Southgate. Following a reported fallout with former assistant coach Steve Holland, the Arsenal defender stepped away from international duty for personal reasons.

Although he recently suggested supporters would not react negatively if they knew the full story, White has refused to throw anybody under the bus . He was previously targeted by the crowd upon his initial return to the setup in March, before missing the subsequent World Cup due to injury.

Despite the audible dissent at Wembley, Tuchel claimed he missed the negative reaction entirely. The England boss instead expressed a desire for supporters to draw a line under the past and fully embrace the defender.

"I didn't hear the boos, to be honest," Tuchel said. "I heard the claps for Luka Modric, which is nice because he deserves it, he's a legend of the game, but I honestly didn't hear the boos for Ben. I thought we were past that chapter. I hope it doesn't happen again. He's a player of ours."

The German tactician emphasised the defender's immaculate attitude since returning to the international fold.

Tuchel added: "Since I'm in charge, he's desperate to come and to be with the group. He doesn't put a foot wrong since I'm in charge. I can only judge him on what I see and what I experienced, and it is on the highest level, and he can really help us to win football matches. Like I said, he's part of our group, and we will protect our group, and are protective of our group. He deserves to be with us and, yeah, I hope we can open a new chapter for him."

When questioned if the continued hostility might prompt White to permanently walk away from international football again, Tuchel quickly dismissed the prospect.

"I don't think so. I don't want to make it bigger than it is. I don't think so, I don't hope so," Tuchel explained. "He seemed to me always committed and always dedicated and excited to come into camp and get the call-up. He had too many injuries. He's a high-quality player, and I honestly don't even know what happened and what were the deep reasons in the situation that he left camp."

Reiterating his absolute faith in the Arsenal star, the manager stated: "So, like I said, (since) I'm in charge, there is no reason to doubt his commitment or passion. I don't want to think in these extreme terms at the moment. He overcame the boos the last time. I didn't hear them this time and he can play on a high level. He proves it week in, week out for Arsenal."

White's situation was ultimately a sideshow on a night that saw England secure their place in March's Nations League quarter-finals. Morgan Rogers' opener and a match-winning penalty from Harry Kane - on his record-breaking 126th appearance - cancelled out Petar Sucic's effort for the visitors.

The Three Lions now travel to face Group A3 leaders Spain on Sunday, knowing a victory will secure top spot.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino tactics: Can Argentine solve Man Utd's problems?
articles.summary: With Mauricio Pochettino set to become Man Utd manager, we analyse if he can clear the tactical hurdles others haven't.
articles.body:
When Mauricio Pochettino was asked the three Premier League managers he would have loved to have played for, he was unequivocal.

"Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson," replied Pochettino, who is set to be the next manager of Manchester United .

In 2023, the Argentine - then at Chelsea , and dressed in full Blues training gear - was being interviewed by Sky Sports. Still he felt a need to express his adoration for Ferguson.

Six years prior to that interview, while managing Tottenham , he had shared lunch with the legendary former United manager.

"When I was young, when I started my career as a manager, he was always my inspiration, my reference," Pochettino said.

"And when you can share two hours with a person who was the greatest manager in the history of football, you can only enjoy."

Hiring United managers has been complicated since Ferguson's departure in 2013, and one of the most prominent complications has been a back-and-forth around the club's DNA.

For some, winning by any means necessary should take precedence, while others believe the style of play and cultural heritage of United's most successful period is vital to the club's identity.

In recent years, United's managerial merry-go-round has alternated between European coaches with their own fixed styles of play, and former players from the Ferguson era.

But between his tactics of choice and his adoration for the former United boss, Pochettino may be uniquely placed to bridge the gap between both camps.

Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better

Michael Carrick's United produced a series of good results to finish last season with a run unmatched by any other team in the league. They looked great, but it was a greatness built on attacking in a transition-heavy manner.

Under Carrick, in games they had less than 50% of the ball, they only lost once. In those 13 games, they boasted a win-rate of 62%. This dropped to 36% in games they had the majority of possession.

This style of play suited their direct attackers and protected their defenders.

At the same time, Casemiro's set-piece prowess provided United a reliable way to break the deadlock against deep defences - something they have struggled with this season.

With United a goal up, opponents stepped forward, giving Carrick's men more space. They could play to their strengths again, attacking quickly. It worked.

But teams at the top are reluctant to play in this way. Carrick's vision for United was a side that played slick football, with short passes in build-up intuitively, referencing Paris St-Germain's midfield three as a source of inspiration.

Building up in this manner, to entice and escape from pressure, before looking to find the forwards quickly, was the plan Carrick was working towards.

This didn't come to fruition and trying to take United from a successful counter-attacking side to one that could reliably beat teams while keeping the ball was the same hurdle that undid Ole Gunnar Solskjar and Erik ten Hag.

Pochettino gives United an interesting solution to this problem.

In his own words, he has described his sides as needing "to be protagonists, always press high, work hard and be dynamic". He refers to himself as a "disciple" of the legendary Argentina boss Marcelo Bielsa, who he played for.

If you wanted an immediate comparison in the Premier League to a coach who resembles Pochettino's ideas in possession, it would be worth looking at Liverpool 's Andoni Iraola, who similarly cites Bielsa as his reference.

These are coaches who, while taking the initiative, encourage vertical football. For as different as the clubs are, both the fans of United and Liverpool have enjoyed success when their teams have played high-octane football.

This summer's World Cup was a strong showcase of Pochettino's style of play and his recent tactical adaptation.

Rather than a fixed, positional style of play - akin to the work of somebody like Manchester City 's Enzo Maresca - Pochettino's USA had only certain players being tasked with holding their position.

This approach posed problems for teams who defended in a zonal manner - defending specific areas rather than individual players.

The US midfielders being able to move freely meant they could step into areas of the pitch between the zones that were being defended, which resulted in their players often being unmarked with time and space on the ball.

By playing in close proximity to each other in the middle of the pitch, the US found another benefit.

Small-space passing combinations helped draw the opposing team up towards the ball and combined with clever off-ball movement to stretch the pitch, allowed the US to find their striker with few defenders around him.

Pochettino's men looked to thread through-balls in behind and early after enticing the opposition's press and the speedy Folarin Balogun was able to turn those chances into goals.

This combination of a fluid midfield, small-space passing and direct through-balls doesn't sound dissimilar to what Carrick was trying to move towards implementing this season.

And although that may worry United fans, the similarity in principles will benefit the players.

"My philosophy is to give a freer style with a good organisation," were Pochettino's words in 2014.

Although philosophically similar, that latter part - a clearer organisation to his freer style - is likely to be what Carrick was unable to reliably offer his players.

For fans of top sides, fast-paced, vertical football tends to be accepted when it comes from a place of being proactive - think Ferguson's United or Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool - wanting to keep the ball, but not passing it for passing's sake.

Fast-paced, vertical football tends to be frowned upon when it comes from a place of conceding possession and defending your own goal for long periods of the match.

The first half of Carrick's stint did appear proactive, while his 4-2-4 press worked well. Leaving four players high was a risk that allowed them to win the ball back and score quickly, but as teams figured this out, United failed to adapt.

There also appeared to be a drop in the team's fitness the longer United went from the departure of ex-boss Ruben Amorim, who left United well conditioned, albeit on the back of a schedule without European football.

Hiring Pochettino will immediately begin the process of turning United into a well-drilled side, capable of applying intense pressure, likely in a co-ordinated manner.

Pochettino enjoyed relative success with Spurs , built on this intensity and co-ordination, that differentiated him from the rest of the league.

With that unique selling point more common now than a decade ago, how he builds on it will dictate how his tenure unfolds.

But watching Brighton this season, he can be assured that an approach founded on intensity off the ball can work in the Premier League in 2026, with Fabian Hurzeler's men second in the league, with the fourth highest average possession, 10 games in.

Pochettino, from a footballing point of view, feels extremely aligned to the values of Ferguson's United, and as a result will implement numerous similarities to the things Carrick wanted, but ultimately failed, to deliver.

His wealth of experience make him a more proven entity than the departing United manager and if he can get his team fit and pressing high, in typically Pochettino fashion, they should see an upturn in form.

Expanding on his managerial approach, while managing Spurs he explained how "the most important thing [was] to create a good shape for players to be comfortable and to show their real qualities".

Rather than relying on pre-defined pattern, he looks to empower individuals to solve attacking problems. Taking this approach means recruitment of top talent matters more than ever.

"He [gave] me the confidence and licence to go where I wanted on the pitch, where I [could] use my strengths," said Cole Palmer, who enjoyed his most productive Premier League season under Pochettino at Chelsea .

United have good attackers but they will need to take the same initiative Palmer did, if platformed to their strengths - something Pochettino does well.

If they don't, and if Pochettino is to stumble, it will likely be in United's inability to break down stubborn defences when asked to dominate the ball - in what would feel like Groundhog Day, again.
