articles.title: Record-breaking Harry Kane sees Luka Modrić’s career as an inspiration
articles.summary: Harry Kane vowed to “push the limits” like inspirational 41-year-old Luka Modrić following his record-breaking England appearance against Croatia. The 33-yea...
articles.body:
Harry Kane vowed to "push the limits" like inspirational 41-year-old Luka Modrić following his record-breaking England appearance against Croatia.

The 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley on Thursday, when a giant tifo hailed 'England's finest' as the captain led the team for his landmark 126th cap.

Kane was given a rapturous reception and displayed the Ballon d'Or to the crowd before a series of presentations centred on him setting a new England's men's appearance record.

The Prince of Wales, William, and previous record holder Peter Shilton led the celebrations on a night that ended with the skipper's spot-kick sealing a 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia under the arch.

"It was incredible, just everything was amazing," said Kane, who admitted he was "trying to play it cool" when he walked out to see a giant banner recognizing his 126th cap.

"A big thank you to everyone who organized it here at the FA, with the tifo and presentations. Thank you to Luka (Modrić) and the Croatian organization for their gift as well.

"Obviously I knew there was going to be something before the game and it was just a special moment.

"It's been a crazy few weeks with a lot happening and of course it's an important moment in our history as a national team, so you have to enjoy these moments.

"But then once the game started, it was just full focus on that.

"I've said before, these occasions feel much better when you win and obviously now I can take a breath and enjoy the whole night itself."

Kane was on the Wembley pitch long after the final whistle with friends and family, who will have undoubtedly further significant moments to celebrate in the years to come.

The striker is now just eight international goals shy of joining the 100 club and plans to play for England until the wheels come off, with fellow Ballon d'Or winner Modrić's longevity providing motivation.

The 41-year-old extended his Croatian appearance record to 207 after coming off the bench at Wembley, where England fans gave him a warm reception.

"He's an inspiration for a lot of us," Kane said. "What an incredible player, but what a great person as well and someone who's looked after himself.

"A great professional and to be playing 40, 41 now, still at this level, is credit to all of his hard work and his mentality.

"So, yeah, that inspires me to push the limits. Like with him, I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you.

"Everyone's journey is different for sure but I've said before that as long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I'm performing at the highest level, then I'll be here for as long as I can.

"Whether that's until I'm 40 or not, we'll have to wait and see. But right now, yeah, I've enjoyed every moment."

Kane's immediate attention is on England's final fixture of the year against World Cup winners Spain in Madrid, where they head having rubberstamped progress to the Nations League quarter-finals.

Thomas Tuchel's side lost 3-2 to Wembley in the Group A3 opener but four straight wins since then gives them hope of finishing top of the pool on Sunday.

"There were things that we can improve on, but it was just about getting the win ultimately," Kane added. "It sets up a fantastic game on Sunday now."

articles.title: Report: €100m-rated Brighton defender dreams of Real Madrid move despite Liverpool interest
articles.summary: Luka Vuskovic has reportedly identified Real Madrid as his ultimate career destination, potentially complicating Liverpool’s pursuit of the Brighton and Hove...
articles.body:
Luka Vuskovic has reportedly identified Real Madrid as his ultimate career destination, potentially complicating Liverpool's pursuit of the Brighton and Hove Albion defender.

According to Sky Sport Germany journalist Florian Plettenberg , Liverpool have placed the 19-year-old on their shortlist for next summer, but the Croatian's long-term ambition is to play at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Vuskovic has made an impressive start to life at Brighton following his move from Tottenham in July.

Understandably, his performances have attracted attention across Europe, with the Premier League club now in a strong position to demand a substantial fee for one of its most promising young players.

Liverpool interest grows as Vuskovic establishes himself at Brighton

Plettenberg reports that Liverpool are monitoring Vuskovic regularly as they assess their defensive options ahead of the summer 2027 transfer window.

Luka Vuskovic dreams of playing for Real Madrid one day. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

The centre-back has firmly established himself under Fabian Hurzeler, strengthening his reputation after an impressive loan spell at Hamburger SV.

Brighton signed him this past summer for a reported £46 million, with a further £4 million in achievable add-ons.

The Croatian agreed a five-year contract running until 2031, and there is no release clause that would allow an interested club to bypass negotiations.

Despite Liverpool's interest, Vuskovic's long-term ambition is to represent Real Madrid one day.

Notably, he is very happy with his development at Brighton, meaning there is no immediate indication that he wants to leave.

Liverpool are closely monitoring Luka Vuskovic. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

However, if he does push for an exit, Brighton are understood to value him at around €100 million, a figure that would be a significant increase on their initial investment.

Real Madrid will undergo defensive overhaul

If Real Madrid are linked with the player in future, it would ideally make sense given their ongoing efforts to build a younger defensive core.

Ibrahima Konate joined the club this summer, while Jacobo Ramon has emerged as a possible longer-term option following his development at Como. However, reports suggest Real Madrid have yet to make a final decision on bringing Ramon back.

Furthermore, with Antonio Rudiger potentially in his final season, the team will indeed need a new centre-back, leaving Vuskovic as a potentially attractive future target, although the financial implications would be considerable.

articles.title: Carlo Ancelotti delivers positive Raphinha update amid Barcelona fitness concerns: ‘Doing very well’
articles.summary: Carlo Ancelotti has offered an encouraging assessment of Raphinha’s condition ahead of Brazil’s friendly against Japan, confirming that the Barcelona forward...
articles.body:
Carlo Ancelotti has offered an encouraging assessment of Raphinha's condition ahead of Brazil's friendly against Japan, confirming that the Barcelona forward is doing well with both club and country.

His comments come as Barcelona monitor the winger's workload during the November international break, with the Catalan club keen to avoid another physical setback after his recent return from injury.

Raphinha, who will captain the national team , has travelled to Singapore for Brazil's two friendlies, against Japan on November 14 and Singapore on November 17.

The number of minutes he receives there will be an important consideration for Barcelona, given his value to Hansi Flick and the injuries that have disrupted his recent availability.

Ancelotti praises Raphinha's form and versatility

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Ancelotti offered a positive assessment of the Barcelona forward's current condition and performances.

Raphinha will captain the national team during November friendlies. (Photo by Ian Hitchcock/Getty Images)

"Raphinha is doing very well here and at Barcelona. He's showing impressive quality at Barça and can play as a striker," said the former Real Madrid boss, according to AS .

Raphinha's fitness remains an important consideration following his recent muscular problems.

As stated earlier, Barcelona and the Brazilian Football Confederation have coordinated to manage his involvement during the two friendlies, reducing the risk of another setback.

However, it is crucial to note that no specific minutes limit has been publicly confirmed.

Meanwhile, Ancelotti also addressed the players' motivation to represent their country, something that was questioned after Raphinha's comments during his contract renewal , stressing the importance of Brazil's status and the support they receive from their fans.

Ancelotti confirms Raphinha is motivated to play for Brazil. (Photo by Albert Perez/Getty Images)

"I know the players want to play for the national team and I don't need to say anything to them to get them out there competing.

"Brazil is the greatest national team in the world and the fans will be right behind us in every match and will support us. It's different in other countries."

Flick will be hoping Raphinha returns without another setback

For Barcelona, it is quite clear that they will want their captain to complete international duty in good condition.

Raphinha's pressing, attacking output and leadership make him an important part of Flick's plans, leaving the club with little incentive to take unnecessary risks with his fitness.

Brazil, meanwhile, have their own reasons to use him carefully. Ancelotti knows the forward is an important attacking option, and managing his minutes will be crucial even for him, as these two matches are mere friendlies.

articles.title: "You can't always play the same way for 90 minutes" – Zidane backs Olise after quiet second half against Italy
articles.summary: Michael Olise struck early to capitalise on a mistake by Gianluigi Donnarumma and give France the lead in Thursday's UEFA Nations League clash against Italy....
articles.body:
Michael Olise struck early to capitalise on a mistake by Gianluigi Donnarumma and give France the lead in Thursday's UEFA Nations League clash against Italy.

However, Olise's influence waned in the second half, as France struggled and ultimately suffered a 3-1 defeat.

Speaking after the game, France coach Zinedine Zidane was unconcerned by Olise's drop in performance, arguing it's only natural that the winger cannot always play at the same level.

He also pointed to the fact that the 24-year-old has scored five goals in his last five games for the national team.

"You can't always play the same way for 90 minutes. He has scored quite a few goals for us across the last two international breaks, and he has been very good. That's what I'm focusing on," Zidane said in defence of Olise at the post-match press conference, via RMC Sport.

"I don't think he was a little less effective in the second half. We were all a little less effective in the second half. And when the team isn't playing as well, it affects individual performances."

Olise and France will be hoping to finish their UEFA Nations League Group A2 campaign with a win when they face Turkey on Sunday.

articles.title: El portero del gol viral de falta: “Courtois es el mejor guardameta de la historia”
articles.standfirst: Iván Martínez, jugador del Numancia, repasa el gol de falta que ha dado la vuelta al mundo y desvela cómo preparó una acción histórica
articles.summary: Iván Martínez, jugador del Numancia, repasa el gol de falta que ha dado la vuelta al mundo y desvela cómo preparó una acción histórica
articles.body: Minuto 43. 1-0 en el marcador e Iván Martínez, portero del Numancia, cruza todo el campo para hacer algo que pocas veces se ve en el fútbol: lanzar una falta directa. Lo que ocurrió después ya es historia. Su golazo se ha hecho viral y ha dado la vuelta al mundo. Pero ¿cómo se gestó una acción tan poco habitual y qué hay detrás de aquel lanzamiento? Hablamos con el protagonista de una de las imágenes más sorprendentes de la temporada. Pregunta. Ha anotado un gol de falta siendo portero y se ha hecho viral. ¿Cómo ha vivido toda esta explosión mediática? R. Lo he vivido como la locura que es, algo inesperado. Estaba trabajado y habíamos hablado de lo que podía pasar, pero esta cobertura mediática y este boom… Imposible. Nunca me lo habría imaginado. P. No hablamos de un remate a la desesperada: era el minuto 43, con 1-0 en el marcador. ¿Qué se le pasa por la cabeza para cruzar todo el campo y disponerse a lanzar la falta? R. Estaba muy preparado y llevábamos esperando una falta frontal durante seis o siete jornadas. No se me pasó por la cabeza nada más allá de lo que tenía que hacer: mirar a la portería, ver un poco dónde estaba situado el balón y pegarle. Sí que había pensado antes del partido que, si la metía, se podía preparar una buena. P. ¿Tenían planeado internamente cómo iban a hacerlo? R. Estaba pensado, sobre todo, para una posible pérdida. Si le pegas a la barrera y toca correr hacia atrás, o si la coge el portero… Estaba preparado, por supuesto. No era algo de decir: «Venga, a ver qué sale». P. ¿Sabía que iba a subir o se lo indicó el entrenador? R. Era una falta un poco escorada y, sobre todo, en el lado de los zurdos. Entonces nos miramos, él debió consultarlo con el segundo entrenador y se planteó si me la daban o no, porque era un poco complicada. Cuando me lo preguntaron, en ese mismo momento me sentí con confianza y se tomó la decisión. P. Por cómo sale el golpeo y, sobre todo, por la seguridad con la que golpea, parece que lleva toda la vida tirando faltas. ¿En los entrenamientos es el mejor lanzándolas? R. Siempre me ha gustado el golpeo de balón. Eso de «vamos a tirar, vamos a ver quién tira mejor», sobre todo después de los entrenamientos. Creo que este año ha pasado de ser algo lúdico a algo serio. Es muy diferente en competición: esa sensación de presión, de tener que estar concentrado. Me ha gustado hacerlo por primera vez y espero que haya más. P. Hay pocos porteros que hayan lanzado faltas a lo largo de la historia, como Chilavert o Rogério Ceni. ¿Se ha inspirado en alguien o ha sido cosa suya? R. No, me he inspirado en golpeos de jugadores de campo desde pequeño. Me daba curiosidad saber por qué cogía efecto el balón, por qué bajaba en tan poco tiempo, por qué le pegaban tan fuerte y, en lugar de ir hacia arriba, bajaba. He conseguido un buen golpeo, parecido al de otros futbolistas, con el que me siento cómodo. Pero nunca me habría esperado que un entrenador me diese esta función. Es algo inusual. P. ¿Y en qué jugadores se ha fijado a la hora de golpear el balón? R. De estos últimos años, en Szoboszlai. Creo que tiene un golpeo de balón muy parecido, aunque el suyo es increíblemente mejor que el mío. También me fijaba en Cristiano durante sus primeros años y en Gareth Bale, que creo que tiene algún golpeo de esos que suben y bajan. P. Más allá de los golpeos y las faltas, ¿se ha fijado en algún portero en particular? R. Cuando era pequeño, en Víctor Valdés y Casillas, por lo que representaban en los Barça-Madrid y con España. Más adelante, en Neuer, que me parece uno de los tres mejores de la historia. También Ter Stegen me parecía espectacular a nivel técnico, ofensivo y un portero muy completo. A Thibaut Courtois lo dejo aparte porque creo que es el mejor de la historia. Ahora me gusta David Raya, al que creo que me parezco o intento parecerme. Es un perfil similar. Y Joan García me parece increíble. P. Ha mencionado a muchos porteros con un gran juego de pies. ¿Realmente importa en el fútbol actual o está sobrevalorado? R. El portero lo que tiene que hacer es parar, intervenir en la fase defensiva. Pero creo que el fútbol ha evolucionado tanto que tener un jugador de campo más influye mucho, y el portero tiene muchas veces la capacidad de encontrar esa superioridad desde atrás. Tener un portero con un buen golpeo de balón ayuda a encontrar esos espacios y a que el delantero pueda controlar mejor. P. El gol se ha llevado todos los focos, pero llevan siete porterías a cero en diez partidos. ¿Cómo gestionan ese nivel defensivo y esa racha? R. Me alegro de que haya pasado esto para darle visibilidad al trabajo que está haciendo el club. Yo, como soriano, me siento muy satisfecho con el trabajo que se está haciendo este año, desde el inicio, la planificación de la plantilla y la dirección general que ha entrado esta temporada. Creo que se están haciendo las cosas muy bien. En el vestuario también lo estamos consiguiendo. A pesar de ser todos nuevos, estamos construyendo una base muy sólida a nivel defensivo. Creo que estamos avanzando muy bien en todos los sentidos, también a nivel ofensivo. Poco a poco estamos marcando más goles. P. Ahora están líderes de la categoría. ¿Cómo afrontan los próximos partidos después de toda esta euforia? R. Con muchas ganas. La semana de trabajo que estamos haciendo después de ganar 6-0 está siendo espectacular. Estamos a un nivel de intensidad altísimo. La victoria en Copa también nos vino muy bien anímicamente y afrontamos lo que viene con total ambición. Creo que estamos en una muy buena posición. Tenemos dos partidos fuera de casa y sabemos que puntuar lejos de nuestro estadio vale el doble. Ahora tenemos al Valladolid como rival. Si sacamos los tres puntos allí, podemos dar un salto importante en la clasificación. P. Ganaron al Oviedo en Copa en los penaltis. ¿Qué supone eso para un club histórico como el Numancia? R. Es una competición importante para el equipo y para la afición. Desde dentro somos conscientes de que el club lleva unos años inmerecidamente complicados, perdiendo finales de 'play-off', quedándose a las puertas y bajando injustamente. Llevan sufriendo mucho tiempo. En la calle, la gente que conozco me dice que les hemos devuelto esa alegría, esa ilusión por el equipo de su ciudad. Poco a poco, durante los años complicados, se va perdiendo. Desde dentro tenemos que ser conscientes del poder que tenemos, tanto en Liga como en Copa. Es a un partido y pueden pasar mil cosas. Si hemos podido hacerlo contra el Oviedo, ¿por qué no en la siguiente fase? P. ¿Y a qué equipo le gustaría enfrentarse? R. A cualquier equipo de Primera División. Yo jugué en Osasuna de pequeño, en las categorías inferiores. Me encantaría enfrentarme a ellos y encontrarme con viejos amigos. P. El Numancia es un club histórico de Primera División. ¿Pesa en el día a día formar parte de este club? R. Más que pesar, es una responsabilidad. Pero la tienen todos los equipos grandes, no solo el Numancia. Creo que somos un vestuario joven, pero hemos recibido esa responsabilidad como algo positivo, no como algo negativo. Hasta hace dos jornadas estuvimos un mes sin ganar, de manera inmerecida: tres empates y una derrota. Podrían haber surgido dudas, pero, en lugar de eso, el equipo se mantuvo. El equipo dijo: «Yo soy el Numancia, quiero estar primero, quiero estar arriba en esta categoría, quiero ascender». Y lo hemos demostrado. Ganamos en Copa, ganamos en Liga y estamos ahí arriba. P. Se marchó muy joven a Osasuna pero usted es de Ágreda (Soria), ¿Cómo lleva el vínculo con el club y con la ciudad? R. Independientemente de la categoría y de todo lo demás, era el destino al que más ilusión me hacía llegar de todos los que había tenido. Es mi tierra. Lo recibes no solo como una responsabilidad o un reto personal, sino también como una responsabilidad con mis amigos y mi familia. Por ejemplo, Pamplona y Osasuna son muy importantes porque crecí allí y es mi segunda casa. Pero mi primera casa, al final, es Ágreda, es Soria, es mi gente, y creo que se está notando. P. Si estuviera en la última jornada, ¿preferiría volver a marcar un golazo de falta que les diese el ascenso a Primera RFEF o parar un penalti en el minuto 95 para ascender? R. Me quedo con el penalti. Es más difícil meter una falta, pero, al final, el portero lleva el penalti en la sangre. Esa sensación de verlo ahí, de saber que tienes todas las de perder, pero ser consciente o creer que lo vas a parar… Esa sensación, y más aún si vale un ascenso, es una pasada.

articles.title: Raúl se estrena con una promesa: “El Oviedo será valiente y tendrá identidad”
articles.standfirst: El exdelantero debuta como entrenador en el fútbol profesional ante el Girona y pide tiempo para imprimir su sello
articles.summary: El exdelantero debuta como entrenador en el fútbol profesional ante el Girona y pide tiempo para imprimir su sello
articles.body: El estreno de Raúl González Blanco en el fútbol profesional ya tiene escenario y rival: el Carlos Tartiere y el Girona. El nuevo entrenador del Real Oviedo afronta su primera noche en el banquillo azul con una mezcla de ilusión y responsabilidad. “Ojalá sea una victoria, que es la que vamos a pelear”, manifestó en su comparecencia previa, en la que dibujó las líneas maestras del equipo que quiere construir. “Queremos ser un equipo muy presionante, muy vertical”, anunció. El técnico aspira a elevar el ritmo de juego, la intensidad con balón y sin él y la capacidad de mantener un rendimiento constante. No obstante, rebajó las expectativas de una revolución inmediata. “No existen los milagros”, avisó después de una semana de trabajo reducida a apenas unos días. “Una cosa es lo que uno quiere y siente y otra lo que va a suceder mañana”. El exjugador del Real Madrid aseguró que ha encontrado una plantilla receptiva y un entorno que le ha facilitado la adaptación. “Me he encontrado un grupo fantástico a nivel humano”, destacó. Su intervención inicial se ha centrado en conocer a los futbolistas, conservar aspectos que funcionaban con Julián Calero e introducir ajustes puntuales. Reconoció que el anterior Oviedo había ofrecido buenos momentos de fútbol y resultados, pero pretende hacerlo “mucho más equilibrado, mucho más sólido”. La consigna antes de recibir a uno de los candidatos al ascenso es evitar saturar al vestuario. “Los mensajes en estos días han sido muy concretos, muy cortitos”, explicó. Incluso reveló que la charla previa a la sesión apenas había durado diez minutos. Su intención es que los jugadores compitan con seguridad y sepan qué se espera de ellos desde el primer minuto. Raúl evitó ofrecer pistas concluyentes sobre la ubicación de Alberto Reina y defendió que nadie tendrá privilegios por su nombre. “Siempre el equipo estará por encima de todo”, sentenció. También recordó que los suplentes y quienes aprietan durante la semana tendrán un papel importante. En la víspera de su estreno, el entrenador se declaró “feliz y contento” y deseoso de sentir el empuje del Tartiere. Quiere que el público vea un Oviedo “valiente”, comprometido y decidido a buscar el resultado durante los noventa minutos. El desafío inmediato es el Girona; la construcción de su proyecto, insistió, necesitará más tiempo.

articles.title: Barcelona offer fans worldwide chance to have loved ones’ ashes permanently preserved at Camp Nou for €10,000 as stadium revamp bill soars to €2bn
articles.summary: FC Barcelona introduces a unique memorial project at Camp Nou, allowing global fans to have loved ones' ashes permanently preserved in the stadium for €10,000, enhancing their everlasting connection to the club.
articles.body: Barcelona supporters will soon be able to maintain their connection with the club long after their deaths, with the renovated Camp Nou set to include a dedicated memorial where families can place the ashes of loved ones. The project will offer 26,000 spaces for funeral urns, alongside commemorative plaques, allowing supporters from around the world to secure a place at the stadium without needing to be club members. The privilege, however, comes with a range of fees and time-limited concessions.Barcelona plan 26,000 niches in new Camp Nou memorialThe club's Memorial FC Barcelona will occupy a 1,500-square-metre space within Camp Nou, combining a columbarium with an area for commemorative plaques. A columbarium is a dedicated structure containing individual compartments, known as niches, in which funeral urns holding cremated remains can be placed.Designed by architect Quique Montoya, the memorial is being developed in collaboration with the company Mes Que Un Memorial. Its design will feature four large illuminated squares, with urns housed behind a mural depicting significant moments from Barcelona's 125-year history. Commemorative plaques will be displayed on a glass wall illuminated by LED lighting.The club has described the interior as a contemporary space using fine materials and warm lighting, with large murals and visual, audiovisual and sound installations dedicated to its history. Families will be able to choose between placing a loved one's ashes in a niche or having their name and a personal message displayed on a plaque.Both options will be available to Barcelona supporters worldwide, regardless of whether they hold club membership. Concessions will be offered for 10, 25 or 50 years, while a separate option will allow supporters to secure a niche permanently.How much will it cost to have ashes placed at Camp Nou?The cost of a place in the columbarium will depend on the length of the concession. A 10-year arrangement is priced at €2,490 (approximately $2,753), while a 50-year concession will cost €6,000 (approximately $6,634). An annual maintenance fee of €70 (around $77) will also apply.Supporters seeking a permanent resting place can purchase a niche for €10,000 (approximately $11,057). A commemorative plaque is available separately for €490 (around $542) for a standard 10-year arrangement, while a premium plaque lasting 50 years will cost €1,040.Barcelona said interest in the initiative had already come from supporters, club members, former players and relatives of historic figures associated with the institution. More than 1,000 fans have reportedly booked places ahead of the memorial's opening, with their contributions also expected to help fund the stadium redevelopment.Presenting the project, the club's institutional vice-president, María Elena Fort, explained the personal attachment that had inspired the idea. “When my grandfather died many years ago, he said the only thing he wanted was to be buried next to Barça’s pitch so that he could hear the goals go in during the afterlife. Many fans dream of the same thing,” she said.Barcelona are not the first Spanish club to introduce such a facility. Atlético Madrid, Real Betis and Espanyol already have smaller columbaria at their respective stadiums.Camp Nou redevelopment continues as costs approach €2 billionThe memorial forms part of Barcelona's wider modernisation of Camp Nou, a stadium originally built in 1957. The redevelopment began in 2023, with the club aiming to increase capacity from 99,354 to 105,000, making it Europe's largest football stadium and the second largest in the world, behind the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea.The project has faced delays and substantial cost increases. Initially estimated at €900 million (approximately $996 million), the redevelopment bill has since risen to nearly €2 billion (approximately $2.2 billion). The financial burden has also affected supporters, with ticket prices having doubled in recent years for non-season-ticket holders.Barcelona have already returned to their home ground, although its capacity remains restricted while construction of the upper tier continues. The club will have to leave the stadium temporarily again next season while the roof is installed. Once completed, Camp Nou is expected to accommodate 105,000 spectators.The memorial is being developed in two phases, with construction scheduled to begin in late 2027 and the full project expected to be completed by the middle of 2028. The completed stadium is also among three venues being considered to host the 2034 World Cup final, which Spain, Portugal and Morocco are due to co-host. Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu and the Grand Stade Hassan II, under construction near Casablanca with a planned capacity of 115,000, are the other candidates.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vicky López sufre una recaída y estará entre seis y ocho semanas más de baja
articles.standfirst: El pronóstico de su lesión muscular en el recto anterior ha empeorado
articles.summary: El pronóstico de su lesión muscular en el recto anterior ha empeorado
articles.body: La delantera del Barcelona Vicky López ha empeorado de su lesión muscular en el recto anterior de la pierna derecha y estará entre seis y ocho semanas más de baja, según informó este viernes el club catalán. La atacante azulgrana se ha sometido a nuevas pruebas médicas que han determinado que presenta una "reagudización" de su lesión, que ha tenido una "evolución fluctuante y no del todo satisfactoria" en las últimas semanas. El período de baja que establecieron los servicios médicos de la entidad azulgrana fue de unas dos semanas cuando informaron de la lesión de López el pasado 23 de septiembre. La jugadora debía haber reaparecido la semana pasada, pero volvió a notar molestias en la zona afectada. Este nueva evaluación médica ha determinado que la futbolista madrileña deberá estar de baja entre un mes y medio y dos meses más "para garantizar su plena recuperación". Una larga ausencia que se suma a las de otras dos atacantes con las que Pere Romeu tampoco podrá contar hasta mediados de diciembre: la brasileña Kerolin Nicoli y la portuguesa Kika Nazareth, lesionadas en el sóleo y en el recto anterior de la pierna derecha, respectivamente. También sigue de baja la defensa Laia Alexandri, baja desde el 5 de febrero a causa de una rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla derecha y que última su vuelta a los terrenos de juego.

articles.title: Birmingham lead, Middlesbrough's Will Lankshear reliance & West Ham need Scott Parker spark - Championship talking points
articles.summary: Billy Sharp and Luke Chambers ran the rule over the first third of the Championship season on the latest Sky Sports Essential EFL podcast; discussing Birmingham City, Middlesbrough, West Brom, West Ham, Wrexham, Preston and more.
articles.body:
Birmingham City lead the way at the international break, while it is so close in the top half in the promotion and play-off race.

On the latest episode of the Essential EFL podcast from Sky Sports , Bily Sharp and Luke Chambers ran the rule over the key talking points from the second tier...

Birmingham City are top of the Championship after a brilliant run of form under Chris Davies. The Blues have won six of their last seven games, and have been beaten just twice all season.

Billy Sharp: You saw glimpses of it last season, but obviously they haven't had the consistency that they've shown this season. They've done it very quietly, actually. Nobody's really spoken about them.

He's got the two settled centre-halves, which I've liked since last season when I've seen them both. He's playing a 4-2-3-1, which really suits him at the minute. A lot of teams play that system, but he seems to have a settled side and has added a little bit of magic with Liam Millar coming in down one side.

Jay Stansfield got the two goals in their last game, which should do him a world of good because we know he's got the ability. When he gets firing and scoring goals, he can win games for Birmingham.

I'm surprised they're top of the league, honestly, I am. But I think we said something similar about Swansea last time. It's still tight at the top and fair play to Birmingham for going into this international break in top spot. There's a long way to go, though.

I didn't think they'd have the firepower to be around the top of the league. I thought they'd be in and around the play-offs. Maybe having eight play-off places means teams can go out and try to win games away from home because they know they're still in and around the play-offs if they don't get the result.

Rather than going for a point, teams are trying to get that head start. At this stage of the season, I think that's why it's so tight at the top. Teams are just going for it rather than sitting back and trying to stay in the game. As you can see from the stats, Birmingham have got a good defensive record, but they're also scoring goals. Fair play to them, Davies is doing a great job.

Are Middlesbrough too reliant on Lankshear?

It is two games without a goal now for Middlesbrough since star man Will Lankshear picked up his injury. Before then, he had scored 13 in 13 in the Championship.

Luke Chambers: "I think the last two games have shown us that Middlesbrough are heavily reliant on Will Lankshear. There was a time when he had a little spell coming off the bench and scoring, but if they don't have the option of him on the pitch at any stage, there's certainly a big drop-off between him and who's come in.

He gives you energy, pace and tenacity up front, but when you don't have that focal point, you lose something. Most of Lankshear's goals have been one-touch finishes. He's not someone who's creating his own chances. The players are creating the chances and he's putting them away.

You move on to Amario Cozier-Duberry, and he can't continue to assist and score at the rate he has been either. With Lankshear in the side, they have so many threats that everyone has to cover, which leaves space for everyone else who's on top form.

If you take that player out, Tommy Conway has been stop-start this season on the left-hand side as well. Jeremy Sarmiento hasn't quite reached the heights he probably would have liked.

The injuries to Hayden Hackney and Morgan Whittaker last season really cost them that automatic promotion shot. They couldn't score a goal. That would be the worrying thing for me, if it started repeating itself.

We're at the stage now where this is the first time we're questioning Middlesbrough. So far, we've been so impressed with them. Everyone's waxed lyrical about how efficient and dangerous they've been, and how much they've learned from the disappointment of last season, when they weren't creating and scoring enough chances.

Without Lankshear, they've obviously missed him. We can put it down to the coincidence of two games, but the most goals someone else has scored is three. He's on 13, and it shows you the massive disparity that isn't spread throughout the side.

That would be a concern for me. The more we talk about it, the more pressure builds on Middlesbrough. The players subconsciously start to think about it again and about those things repeating themselves. They'll need to quieten that down a little bit.

Hopefully, after the international break, they can bounce back. He'll hopefully be nearly ready to go again. But when you're relying on one individual after what happened to them last season, those subconscious thoughts can start creeping in. You might think in the back of your mind that you can't let this happen again.

West Brom narrowly staved off relegation last season, but they have been exceptional under James Morrison so far in this campaign. They are fifth in the table and just a point off top.

BS: They've been up there, in and around where they are, since the start of the season. I had the opportunity to speak to Isaac Price in an interview a few weeks ago and get a little bit of inside information about what James Morrison has been like.

It seems to me like he's giving that group of players a lot of freedom and belief to just go and express themselves. Obviously, they've got a philosophy, a way of playing and tactics, but they've got some special young players who seem to be really loving playing football at the minute.

Price is one of them, scoring big goals for them. Whenever I see him, I always wonder what position he's playing because he's popping up all over the pitch. He's somebody who's thriving with his game at the minute and has got a lot of self-belief.

When I spoke to him, he backed himself and really believes in his team-mates as well. To me, it looks like Morrison is giving that group a really happy dressing room. Price also said the lads really love playing under Morrison, so it seems to be a good recipe at the minute.

He knows the club inside out and has definitely got the fan's backing. It just seems to be going really smoothly, from the fans to what's happening on the pitch with the players.

Even when they've had a bad result, you've seen that they're working for their manager. There doesn't seem to be any unrest in the camp and there's no negative talk in the media about West Brom. Everything we talk about with West Brom is positive, about good, young, hungry players.

Just a point so far for Scott Parker in his brief tenure in charge at West Ham. They fought back for an unlikely point at Cardiff in a 3-3 draw in his first game in charge, before going on to lose 2-1 at Blackburn. After 15 games, the Hammers find themselves sat outside the top eight.

LC: I think he'll be pleased that he ultimately did take on the Cardiff game when it shocked everyone. I was actually covering that game and they went 3-0 down by half-time. I just couldn't believe my eyes, that a group of players at that level, with that much ability and playing for that football club, could put in a performance like that.

Thankfully, he was able to give that team talk, make the changes at half-time and they got themselves back into it.

We all know, and he'll know, that when you go anywhere in this league, it doesn't matter who you are. Especially when you're going to West Ham, as Blackburn Rovers did, players raise their game. Me and Billy have been there. You play against teams on a better run and you're expecting more of yourself sometimes, so you raise your game to another level.

That's what West Ham are going to have to get used to. There's going to be a media circus following Scott Parker's appointment and the story of him going back there after being a player at the club. But he'll certainly understand the task ahead of him.

He needs to change the mindset and probably the culture in the group because they've been used to losing for a few seasons now. We all expected them to bounce straight back and at least be further up the table.

These two results, a draw and a defeat, have damaged their league position. When Nuno was let go, they weren't too far off it. They're still only six points away from the top two and well within the fight for a play-off place. There's a long, long way to go.

This international break will have come at the perfect time for him and his players to have a reset and for him to get his ideas across. It's still going to be a massive job because he's got to get the fans back onside and give them some sort of impression that this side can achieve everything everyone is desperate to achieve. The only goal is promotion for West Ham this season.

It has been an underwhelming start to the season for Wrexham. Phil Parkinson's side sit in the bottom half, having won just four of their first 15 games.

BS: I don't think it's the Wrexham of last season. They've brought in so many players that some of them are probably still learning the way Wrexham play.

I go back to two or three weeks after they got beaten at Sheffield United. I was really looking forward to that game because I thought it was going to be a big occasion. There seems to be a bit of rivalry between the two, but there was no needle whatsoever. There were no tackles and no real urgency from Wrexham. They were passive in the press and had some big players missing.

They didn't put balls into the box for Kieffer Moore to get on the end of and didn't really do anything to Sheffield United. It was pretty comfortable for Sheffield United in the end.

Phil Parkinson said some strong words in the press afterwards. He wasn't throwing the players under the bus, but he said that wasn't the Wrexham he wanted to see. It was probably the worst Wrexham performance he'd seen in many years.

He definitely got a reaction because they've picked up a little bit since then.

I think they've had a big turnaround of players and, whenever I see that team, I always wonder if there are going to be changes in the next game. I just don't think they're quite settled.

It was a huge win last time out for Preston. They claimed a first three points under Graham Alexander as they beat Southampton 1-0 at Deepdale. But they are still bottom of the Championship, and seven points adrift of safety.

LC: What a result that was. Who saw that one coming? Southampton have been absolutely flying.

Under Graham Alexander, I think he was always going to need time with this group of players. You talk about a team and where they want to be, where they expect to be and where the fanbase expects them to be.

I can only relate it to this time when I was at Ipswich, where it was probably underfunded for so long. There was a lack of vision to drive things forward and a lack of a really clear plan.

We ended up falling out of the league because we signed players who we hoped would step up from a division, and we weren't able to replace the ones who were proven at that level.

I look at the squad now at Preston and I do fear the worst for them, for Graham Alexander going in there. Yes, it's a fairytale for him going back to the club where he played so many games, but sometimes I really don't see where the miraculous turnaround is going to come from.

I don't want to write them off, but I do think it's going to be a really tough time for them over the next few months to try to stay in the Championship. For me, that's the only thing they're playing for at this stage of the season.

articles.title: La apelación del Manchester City ya tiene fecha... y la sanción también
articles.standfirst: La vista se llevará a cabo a mediados de diciembre y, si no prospera, habrá decisión en enero
articles.summary: La vista se llevará a cabo a mediados de diciembre y, si no prospera, habrá decisión en enero
articles.body: El juicio que tiene en vilo al fútbol inglés (y al europeo) está cada vez más cerca de escribir su punto final. El Manchester City, declarado culpable por un panel independiente de infringir las normas financieras de la Premier League, podrá defenderse a mediados de diciembre, según informa Financial Times. La apelación del Manchester City, que tratará de revocar todos los cargos de los que ha sido acusado y declarado culpable, podría durar varios días según el diario financiero, que asegura que se espera que "la comisión independiente dicte sentencia sobre dicha apelación a principios del próximo año, seguida de una decisión sobre las sanciones". Es decir, que según el calendario planteado, una vez que la comisión decida sobre la apelación del club citizen, algo que sucederá a principios de enero, la sanción se podría hacer pública de manera casi inmediata. Eso sí, insiste el Financial Times, no está claro cuándo entrarían en vigor unos castigos que, además, serían apelables, lo que alargaría aún más un proceso que ya lleva años enturbiando el fútbol inglés. Sobre la posible sanción se ha escrito mucho y se conoce poco. Las últimas informaciones desde Inglaterra apuntaban a que el castigo más probable sería una deducción de puntos lo bastante grande como para garantizar el descenso a la Championship, junto a una multa muy elevada... y una segunda deducción para la siguiente temporada que imposibilitara o, al menos, dificultase, el ascenso inmediato a Premier. Aunque la Premier parecía decidida a buscar una sanción incluso antes de que se conociera el resultado de la apelación, la información del Financial Times va en dirección opuesta e invita a pensar en un calendario más sereno y menos acelerado.

articles.title: Nations League 2026/27: England into quarter-finals but who will they play in last-eight in March?
articles.summary: Nations League quarter-finals, semi-finals and final format explained, with draw for last eight in November after groups decided; England have progressed to knockouts but can win group with victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday
articles.body:
Top spot still up for grabs - and could be key

England are currently second in Nations League Group A3 behind Spain, trailing the world champions by three points.

Thomas Tuchel's side lost to Spain at Wembley at the start of this campaign and have their final match of the group stage in Madrid on Sunday.

Both sides are assured of a quarter-final place but a win for England will mean they finish top of the group.

That matters as the winners of the Nations League tier A groups are seeded for the quarter-final draw. They will play teams which have finished runners-up in other groups. They will also play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

If England draw or lose against Spain, they will finish second and face a group winner in March.

Who could England face in the quarter-finals?

After matches on November 12, the sides below are in contention for a quarter-final qualifying place in the three other tier A Nations League groups:

Group A4: Portugal, Denmark, Wales, Norway

The draw for the last eight will take place on November 20 at 11am.

When are the quarter-finals and how do they work?

The quarter-finals will be two-leg ties, with the seeded group winners playing the second match at home.

The matches will take place in the March international break, with the first legs between March 25-27 and the second legs between March 28-30.

The Nations League Finals will then be held between June 9 and June 13, 2027.

The tournament will feature two semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final, with four nations competing to be crowned champions of Europe.

The four semi-finalists will be invited to make bids to host the semi-finals and final.

articles.body:
The ESPN College Gameday crew is heading to the blue tundra of the Boise State Broncos on Saturday for the No. 24 team's showdown with the high-flying Oregon State Beavers.

Find out when you can check out the premier pre-game show in college football, who the guest picker will be, and a prediction for the big game, in this preview of the Week 11 presentation.

Crew: Rece Davis, Nick Saban, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit, "Stanford" Steve Coughlin, Jen Lada, Jess Sims, and Pete Thamel

Two of the best offenses in college football will square off Saturday night when the Oregon State Beavers visit the No. 24 Boise State Broncos.

The home team possesses one of the finest run games in the country, averaging 237.1 rushing yards per game, good enough for seventh in the nation. The Broncos' offense is the tenth highest-scoring unit in all of college football, averaging 39 points per game.

The visitors have the best passing game in college football, averaging 370.4 yards through the air. They average 38 points per game, the 12th best in football.

The biggest issue facing the Beavers, though, is the status of starting quarterback Braden Atkinson, who is listed as doubtful entering Saturday's game, thanks to a hand issue suffered in a loss to Texas State two weeks ago.

Similarly, Boise State quarterback Maddux Madsen is listed as questionable for the game after sustaining a knee injury in a one-point win over Texas State. Head coach Spencer Danielson confirmed Madsen has participated in practice this week.

The injury to Atikinson, the unreliable accuracy of Maalik Murphy, and the extraordinary play of Broncos running back Dylan Riley make for a long night for the Oregon State squad.

There should still be considerable amounts of scoring, but Boise State will pull away in the second half and control the ball with their rushing attack just enough to score the win with the ESPN crew in town.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino appointed as Manchester United head coach after Michael Carrick's sacking at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as new Man Utd head coach; the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris St-Germain boss will oversee his final two games as USA manager before heading to Manchester; United sacked Michael Carrick with club in Premier League relegation zone
articles.body:
Pochettino will begin the role on Wednesday, after taking charge of the USA's fixtures against Haiti, having signed a deal signed until the summer of 2029.

He is set to meet his new players and take training for the first time on Thursday and his first match in charge will be against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday November 22, live on Sky Sports.

Sky Sports News understands United have to pay around £7.4m to buy Pochettino out of his newly-signed contract with the USA.

In a statement announcing Pochettino's appointment, Man Utd highlighted the Argentinian's reputation for "high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players".

"Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues," the club added.

Pochettino is yet to win major silverware in England. He led Tottenham to a League Cup and Champions League final during his celebrated time in charge, before going on to win the French Cup and Ligue 1 during his one-and-a-half seasons at PSG.

Carrick was sacked after overseeing the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season, leaving United in the relegation zone after 10 matches.

The Manchester United Supporters' Trust called upon the club to back Pochettino following his appointment.

"We warmly welcome Mauricio Pochettino to the club," they said. "When he arrives in Manchester, he will find a fanbase that, whilst furious with the owners, always gives the manager and team on the pitch full-throated support. We now hope the club backs the new manager and gives him all the power, resources and tools he needs to succeed."

Pochettino had previously been linked with the Man Utd job and, following a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday between club chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox and owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to finalise the next steps, the 54-year-old is now set to return to the Premier League as United manager.

Pochettino was the unanimous choice recommended by the club's hierarchy, which was then approved by the club's ownership.

Reports that surfaced Thursday evening about differing preferences between the club's leadership and ownership over the club's next head coach have been described as categorically false by club sources.

As Sky Sports News reported on Thursday, Pochettino was the only coach the club spoke to directly about the position, despite speculation about other potential candidates.

Pochettino will meet his new bosses for the first time in Manchester on Wednesday afternoon/evening

United's squad returns to training for the first time on Thursday after the international break - where they will meet their new head coach for the first time

Pochettino will then have three training days before his first match in charge of United, away at Liverpool on Sunday

Liverpool (A) - Premier League - Sunday November 22, live on Sky Sports

Sporting (A) - Champions League - Wednesday November 25

Brentford (H) - Premier League - Saturday November 28

Newcastle (A) - Premier League - Wednesday December 2, live on Sky Sports

Coventry (H) - Premier League - Saturday December 5

RB Leipzig (H) - Champions League - Tuesday December 8

Pochettino to be backed in January transfer window

Sky Sports News Rob Dorsett on whether Mauricio Pochettino will be backed in January:

"I think he will be backed considerably. Man Utd try and do their business in the summer transfer windows because they've still got a number of players they want to move out. Part of the reason they didn't spend as much in the transfer window just gone was because they couldn't get a number of players out.

"They were expecting to get £36m for Marcus Rashford as part of a contract they had with Barcelona. Barcelona then decided not to go through with that and go for Anthony Gordon instead.

"The big thing for Pochettino this summer is a lot of players are out of contract. You're talking Harry Maguire, Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw. All of them have an option in Manchester United's favour to extend that by a year.

"A lot of these players are on huge wages. Bruno Fernandes is the biggest earner behind Marcus Rashford. The two biggest earners, both of whom are out of contract in the summer."

The former Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea boss brings Premier League experience to the Man Utd job but what do his previous roles tell us about how his team might shape up at Old Trafford?

From his tactical blueprint at Southampton to youthful dynamism at Spurs and adapting at Paris Saint-Germain, Sky Sports' Nick Wright analyses what to expect from Pochettino.

articles.title: Ranking Cavan Sullivan and the Rising Stars of the USMNT
articles.summary: One word has defined the U.S. men's national team's early steps toward the 2030 FIFA World Cup: youth.
articles.body:
One word has defined the U.S. men's national team's early steps toward the 2030 FIFA World Cup: youth.

For the USMNT's first camp after their defeat to Belgium in the World Cup round of 16 this past summer, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino called up 13 players awaiting their senior international debuts.

All 13 debuted in a four-game window that featured friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.

Next up for the United States is a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. With several young players again involved, one question is worth asking: Which U.S. talents deserve close attention this month and beyond?

Let's break down the top talents in the United States' pool.

7. Neil Pierre, 19, Center Back, Philadelphia Union

With Tim Ream announcing his retirement during the last international window, the USMNT has a vacancy at center back. Might Neil Pierre, just 19 years old, be the one to fill it?

Standing at 6'7", Pierre is a giant in the backline. His elite defensive range has already made him a standout for the Philadelphia Union and helped him earn his senior international debut during the fall camp.

Pierre can chase down balls in behind his own backline like no other player at the USMNT's disposal. He has a bit of refinement to do yet when it comes to his defensive decision-making, but that should come with experience.

Pierre also offers an astonishing goal threat from set pieces. He scored five goals in just 1,560 MLS regular-season minutes for Philadelphia, adding another dimension to his case for a prominent USMNT role.

While Pierre's distribution is a work in progress, he's chock full of promising tools that could pay dividends for the national team.

6. Justin Ellis, 19, Striker, Orlando City

Justin Ellis scored multiple goals in his first U.S. camp. He bagged one on his debut against Peru to begin the window and scored a gutsy strike against Canada while nursing an injury suffered earlier in the match.

Those goals illustrate Ellis' budding potential in the box as a true striker — but likely weren't the things that drew the attention of Pochettino and his coaching staff in the first place.

The Orlando City youngster's best skill is his work on the ball. A brilliant passer, combiner and carrier, Ellis brings a level of comfort in possession matched by perhaps no one else in the U.S. player pool outside of Gio Reyna. Even when stuck in the tightest of corridors, the 19-year-old seems to always find an escape route.

Whether his future with the USMNT is as a lone striker or as some sort of second forward or attacking midfielder, Ellis has the on-ball nous to play a major role moving forward.

5. Mathis Albert, 17, Winger, Borussia Dortmund

For a moment, Mathis Albert's name was in the record books. With his goal in the United States' victory over Chile in September, the Borussia Dortmund teenager became the youngest scorer in USMNT history.

Then, a few days later, Sullivan rewrote the record books with his strike against Mexico.

Don't let the turning tides of history fool you, though. Albert is a player to watch. Though his lone start of the September-October window didn't result in fireworks, he was a spark plug off the bench in the USMNT's other three contests.

With his smooth dribbling, the 17-year-old can glide through opposing defensive shapes with ease. He's also a savvy mover off the ball, making smart runs either in behind or into spaces between the lines.

Albert is still settling in at Dortmund, but few players in the U.S. pool are better equipped to pull off slaloming runs and tight turns under pressure.

4. Peyton Miller, 18, Left Back/Left Winger, New England Revolution

Entrusted with a start in the USMNT's first game of this new World Cup cycle, Peyton Miller quickly looked up to the level of the international game.

Of course, there are much sterner tests out there than Peru, a team the U.S. beat 4-1 in September. But at least one thing was clear from Miller's first taste of the senior national team and from his minutes with the New England Revolution: he is quick .

One of the fastest players in MLS, his blazing speed has been a huge part of his success across multiple positions.

Used by Pochettino as a left back in his lone start, Miller has played more as a winger than a fullback for New England manager Marko Mitrovic. He played as a winger at times for the U.S. in the last camp, too.

Thanks to his mixture of pace, goal threat and vision, Miller posted 14 goal contributions in the regular season. Although a lower-body injury makes him the lone player on this list missing the USMNT's November window, he won't be in MLS for much longer.

3. Julian Hall, 18, Striker, Red Bull New York

One of the standouts of the United States' first post-2026 World Cup camp, Julian Hall bagged a trio of goals in the fall window.

Those three strikes came in back-to-back-to-back games, making the teenage forward just the third player in USMNT history to notch a goal in each of his first three games in the red, white and blue.

Hall's nose for goal is undeniably his finest quality. With clever movement inside the box and a willingness to throw himself at service, the 18-year-old already has a knack for putting the ball in the back of the net.

Hall is more than just a poacher, though. With underrated skill on the ball, he's been used as a winger and as a No. 10 at times by Red Bull New York manager Michael Bradley—who knows a thing or two about the USMNT—this season in MLS.

His best position is clearly as a No. 9, but Hall has been trusted to deputize elsewhere points to his varied skill set. He's also a tenacious presser, which should endear him to any manager he crosses paths with during his career.

2. Adri Mehmeti, 17, Defensive Midfielder, Red Bull New York

It's entirely possible that the United States has never produced a men's prospect like Adri Mehmeti.

The 17-year-old, who earned his first USMNT call-up in the fall window, has unparalleled comfort on the ball at the base of midfield. A smooth defensive midfielder who grew up idolizing Sergio Busquets, he became an every-game starter for Red Bull New York in his first season of top-division soccer.

You can see why Michael Bradley has entrusted him with such a big role so quickly. Mehmeti is far more likely to dazzle on the ball than any deep-lying midfielder in modern USMNT history. Just look at how he swept past a World Cup winner in Rodrigo De Paul in the Red Bulls' impressive 2-0 win over Inter Miami last month:

Mehmeti's defensive work still has room to grow, but with his smart positioning off the ball and his brilliant work on it, he looks like a star in the making.

1. Cavan Sullivan, 17, Winger, Philadelphia Union

The youngest goalscorer in USMNT history, Cavan Sullivan announced himself on the international stage during the fall window. His left-footed chipped goal from well outside the box against Mexico was the standout moment of the four games.

That Sullivan has already been entrusted with multiple starts by Pochettino speaks to how highly the new Manchester United head coach views him. The Argentine is certainly not alone in that assessment.

Having already agreed to a Manchester City deal that will trigger a move after his 18th birthday, Sullivan has been in great form for the Philadelphia Union this season. Ranked No. 1 on MLS's 22 Under 22 list , he averaged a staggering 0.79 non-penalty goal contributions per 90 minutes in the regular season.

With top-tier dribbling ability, ball-striking and passing vision, Sullivan is already one of the best attackers on this side of the Atlantic. The future is blindingly bright.

articles.title: Arsenal vs London City Lionesses: Have Renee Slegers' side lost the fear factor of playing at the Emirates Stadium?
articles.summary: Arsenal are yet to win any of their four WSL home games this season; With insight from captain Kim Little and Renee Slegers, Arsenal have set out how they are going to change this; watch Arsenal vs London City Lionesses live on Sky in the WSL this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
The lack of home wins has cut the Gunners adrift from the WSL title race. But more worryingly, the message is getting round the league that Arsenal are not as invincible as before in their 60,000-seater stadium.

"Many players have said it's one of the hardest places to go to in the WSL," said Nikita Parris to Sky Sports' Pitch to Pod show.

"And at the moment, teams are taking points off them at home. Teams feel like when they go there, they have a chance.

"At times [in the past], you go to the Emirates, they suffocate you. It's so different. Now teams they can see they can get a counter attack that builds a bit of momentum and you're thinking: 'if one of these go in….'. And at times they have been going in.

"In games, we give ourselves a chance - whereas in previous times Arsenal have never allowed that."

These comments were put to Arsenal captain Kim Little at the club's training ground. The response is defiant.

"That's obviously a reflection of these results at the start of this season," she tells Sky Sports . "But I think historically at the Emirates, we're hard to play against. It's our place.

"That doesn't disappear overnight. We've not had the results we want there, we know we're capable of it. And we want to do that in our next game."

Lo and behold, Parris and her London City Lionesses team are next up at the Emirates this weekend, live on Sky Sports . And it's a game that puts Arsenal's season very much at a crossroads.

With the WSL title seemingly out of their grasp on current form, Arsenal will look to muster a top-three finish for a Champions League spot - but London City are threatening to snatch that from them.

Should Arsenal win on Sunday, they would be breathing down the necks of the WSL's big-spending surprise package. Defeat, however, would open up a nine-point gap between Arsenal and London City.

In just a 26-game season, that's a huge mountain to climb - especially when up against a team in form.

Arsenal have shown resilience this week to beat Liverpool, then claim a draw at Barcelona. But can they turn their confidence away from home into a first Emirates win this season?

Why have Arsenal struggled so much at home?

If Arsenal players have been listening to Parris' comments, then her words should be put up on the wall of the dressing room ahead of Sunday's match. But the Gunners have to do more than just motivate themselves to a crucial home win.

There are tactical elements to this slump in form. After all, head coach Slegers agrees with Parris' analysis.

"I think the fact that one team gets success the way they do it at the Emirates has built belief into other teams doing similar things and stopping us and frustrating us," said Slegers last week.

"There's a piece of that belief building in opposition as well. That's what we've created ourselves, which we have to manage."

But there is one area where Slegers disagrees with Parris' claims. Teams still fear Arsenal at home, otherwise why would they set up so deep?

"What I see when teams come to the Emirates is they come to the Emirates to stop us," she added. "So I think that's a sign of fear for me.

"But they've also seen that there's opportunities to go out on one or two breaks and getting a goal against us. So that's definitely something we need to change."

Little gives a bit more insight into the Arsenal players' mindset about playing at home. "I think players set up on low blocks," she says. "They want to defend and then play on the counter more often, which I suppose is in a way a show of respect to us in our previous seasons.

"We've obviously taken a little dip in that sense of who we are there, but we're working hard and doing all we can to make sure we change those draws into wins, and to be more resourceful."

And there are many ways in which Arsenal can become more resourceful. Despite sitting in sixth place and 12 points off the top of the table, they rank second for possession and number of shots taken.

And despite all that pressure, there are not enough Arsenal players are contributing to their attack. Seven out of their last eight goals in all competitions have been scored by Alessia Russo.

They have the third-worst shooting accuracy record in the division this season, plus the lowest shot conversion rate out of any team. That is what gives opponents the belief that Arsenal can be stopped.

"We've had really dominant displays but got caught on the counter and gone down a goal, which isn't ideal but ultimately that happens." says Little.

"When we play at the Emirates, it's about atmosphere, they're incredible fans, they're supporting us, an incredible arena. And we need to make sure we use that, that we connect, and we're all doing this together.

"Alongside that, obviously there are the more tactical elements, how we can get to the point of the fine details what small things we just need to improve on, or improve the quality of one. So that those chances or the opportunities we're creating are turning into goals."

While Arsenal have struggled at home, Little is keen to point out in their last three home matches - they have fought back from behind to salvage draws. While there are fears about Arsenal's season, there is also fight.

"We're passionate, we invest a lot into what we do every day on a daily basis - as players, as staff, as a broader club, as supporters," says the Arsenal captain.

"So yeah, it does hurt and we expect more from ourselves. But also, sometimes things don't always go as you planned, or the way that you want them to in life - and there are those ebbs and flows.

"So I think how we respond and how we move forward is what says the most about us, and that's what we're trying to do from within.

"And when I look at that and when I look at us and what we're trying to do to get through this patch at the start of the season - which is not what we expect of ourselves here at Arsenal, I'm proud of that.

"We're moving forward, we're taking steps, but yeah, I'm looking forward to the rest of the season."

And as for London City Lionesses? "The season's long, we'll see what happens."

Can Arsenal make it 'ugly and hard' for London City?

For all of Arsenal's woes this season, they are still unbeaten at home in the WSL for over two years.

The last time they lost at home came in September 2024, when Arsenal lost 2-1 to Chelsea. It was Jonas Eidevall's final game in charge, before Slegers took over the ship.

Arsenal have stuck with Slegers despite this early season disappointment. Could a rare home defeat spell the end of her time in charge?

"It's difficult for them you know," added Parris about Arsenal. "For me, that's where Arsenal shine. At the Emirates is where they are so dominant.

"That's got to be a place where teams are coming and thinking: 'Not today. We're not getting a performance there. It's going to be ugly and hard."

The gauntlet has been laid. Arsenal have to make this game "ugly and hard" for London City Lionesses.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino, Manchester United Agree to Contract as Michael Carrick's Replacement
articles.summary: Manchester United has finalized terms on a contract with United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino, the club announced on Friday.
articles.body:
Manchester United has finalized terms on a contract with United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino, the club announced on Friday.

The Athletic's David Ornstein first reported Pochettino and the club had agreed on a contract until the summer of 2029, with his arrival expected ahead of the Nov. 22 match against Liverpool, one of the Red Devils' biggest rivals.

As for Pochettino's replacement, former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola is a reported target , and U.S. Soccer is bound to evaluate the best tacticians in MLS.

"Steve Cherundolo will lead the team's previously scheduled December camp, which will feature a primarily MLS-based roster," the USMNT said. "The camp will reflect the increased alignment between the senior and Olympic programs, and there will not be a separate Under-23 camp in December."

Even before United officially sacked Michael Carrick, Pochettino emerged as the favorite to take over, and an agreement looked like a foregone conclusion.

Pochettino had a hugely successful spell at Tottenham Hotspur. Spurs were runners-up in the 2018-19 Champions League final. In the previous three seasons, the finished third, second and third in the Premier League.

Pochettino was sacked in November 2019, and Tottenham has spent the intervening years chasing the heights it enjoyed during his tenure.

Beyond just the results, the 54-year-old had Spurs playing an entertaining style built around younger stars, many of whom had risen up the youth ranks.

One source of concern is that Pochettino, like Tottenham, is to some degree still trying to equal what he achieved in North London. He won a Ligue 1 title in 2021-22 with Paris Saint-Germain but clashed with some of the biggest stars. He proved to be an equally poor fit at Chelsea and left after just one season.

The memory of Pochettino a lot of fans in England have may not be the manager he is now.

The wider question is whether Manchester United is too big of a job for almost anyone right now.

It's difficult to say anything new regarding the cycle of dysfunction that started the moment Sir Alex Ferguson retired in May 2013.

The players have changed. The managers have changed. There's even a new voice at ownership level guiding the football decisions. And still, the same problems have plagued United time and again.

Center back Lisandro Martínez summed it up with his viral post-match interview following a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League:

It all stems from the top , but the managerial turnover is where the issues are the most acute. Countless millions have been spent on transfers tailored to one specific coach, only for a new coach to come in shortly thereafter and make those players poorly suited for the way he wants to play.

Director of football Jason Wilcox hasn't exactly made a strong account of himself, either, given the general state of the squad. He hasn't built up enough trust to think he could oversee a total overhaul of the team, if one is preferred by Pochettino.

One can see the allure of the Manchester United job given the club's place within world football. Without the necessary structural change, Pochettino may be doomed by the same factors that have felled his predecessors.

articles.title: Man United hires Mauricio Pochettino, who leaves U.S. job with task of reviving former power
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino was hired as Manchester United’s head coach on Friday, agreeing to leave his job with the U.S. national team to take on the challenge of reviving the fortunes of English soccer’s once dominant force.
articles.body: FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. — Mauricio Pochettino was hired as Manchester United’s head coach on Friday, agreeing to leave his job with the U.S. national team to take on the challenge of reviving the fortunes of English soccer’s once dominant force. Just three months after announcing a contract to lead the Americans through the 2030 World Cup, the U.S. Soccer Federation said Pochettino will depart next next week for Old Trafford. The 20-time English champion is in the relegation zone after 10 games of the Premier League season. He will take over ahead of the Nov. 22 match at Liverpool, becoming United’s eighth permanent coach or manager since club great Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. United announced the hiring of the 54-year-old Argentine one day after firing Michael Carrick, who led the team to one Premier League win, five draws and four losses for its worst league start in 40 years. It is 18th in England’s 20-team top division. Pochettino and his assistants will remain with the U.S. team for the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino announced as new Manchester United manager
articles.summary: Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick, who was sacked after United’s disastrous start to the season.
articles.body:
Manchester United have appointed ⁠⁠Mauricio Pochettino as the new manager to replace the ⁠ sacked Michael Carrick , as the Premier League ⁠giants sit in the relegation zone after their worst start to a league ‌campaign in 40 years.

Pochettino will lead the United States national team in their upcoming matches against Haiti before joining ⁠Man United, US ⁠Soccer said on Friday.

“The club has reached an agreement with the US ⁠Soccer Federation for Mauricio and ⁠his staff to ⁠be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the ‌US Men’s National Team,” United said in a ‌statement.

Pochettino, a former Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain, Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton manager, was the favourite for the managerial role at Old Trafford ever since rumours about Carrick’s departure hit the headlines.

The 54-year-old arrives at Old ⁠Trafford with United having earned one win and eight points from 10 Premier League games. They are 18th in the standings, one point above bottom side Crystal Palace.

United have won only three of their 15 matches across all competitions.

Pochettino, who returns to club football, had been in charge of the USA national team since 2024, and under him, the cohosts reached the round of 16 at the 2026 FIFA World Cup in North America.

“The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honours of my career,” Pochettino said in a statement.

British media reported United would have to pay substantial compensation to release Pochettino from his US Soccer contract, which had been due to run ⁠until the 2030 World Cup.

Pochettino becomes the eighth permanent man in charge at Man United since Sir Alex Ferguson’s departure in May 2013 after more than 26 years in the job.

United said in their statement that their new manager is known for “his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players”.

Pochettino took charge of Spurs from 2014 to 2019, leading the North London club to the Champions League final in the season before he was sacked.

He guided Spurs to the League Cup final in his first full season and to a runners-up finish in the Premier League in 2017.

Pochettino also spent a season at French giants PSG, leading them to the Ligue 1 title that year, and later guided Chelsea to a League Cup runner-up finish in 2023-2024.

He inherits a Man United squad assembled at considerable expense ⁠but lacking confidence and identity, with supporters booing the players off the pitch after the Bournemouth defeat.

United’s hierarchy, which has often attracted the fans’ criticism, will hope his experience can help stabilise one of football’s most scrutinised clubs.

Pochettino’s first assignment at his new club will be a trip to Anfield to face rivals Liverpool in the league on November 22.
