articles.title: Norway v Wales: Arsenal's Martin Odegaard backs hosts to avenge Cardiff loss
articles.summary: Martin Odegaard backs Norway to brush off snow disruption and avenge their defeat by Wales when they meet again in Oslo on Saturday.
articles.body:
Martin Odegaard admits snow disruption has affected Norway's preparations for Saturday's Nations League meeting with Wales – but the Arsenal captain is backing his team to avenge their defeat in Cardiff last month.

Wales beat the World Cup quarter-finalists 2-1 for their only win of the campaign so far, with Norway head coach Stale Solbakken describing the first-half performance as their worst for two years.

Norway had to train indoors on Thursday because the Ullevaal Stadion pitch, which was criticised earlier this year before being repaired in the summer, was covered in snow.

That snow was cleared on Friday, allowing Norway to resume training in Oslo as they look to climb off the bottom of Group A4.

How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done

Wales' James warns of Norwegian revenge in Oslo

They have three points out of six from four games, the same tally as Wales, but are below Craig Bellamy's side in third because of their head-to-head record.

"Obviously we wanted to train yesterday, so it's not ideal but you have to adapt to the situation, and I think it's not the end of the world," Odegaard said.

On the defeat in Wales, the Arsenal midfielder added: "Our level was not where it should be. I think it's probably the only game for a long time where we haven't been playing to our standards.

"Wales is a good team, a competitive team, lots of good players in big leagues and a physical team as well, and we were prepared for that.

"But I think on the day we were just not showing up to our standards and that's something we want to show tomorrow [Saturday], and we can do a lot better. We want to show a different version tomorrow."

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Having been unbeaten in 2025 before impressing with their run to the last eight at this summer's World Cup, Norway have lost their past three matches , with 2-1 defeats against Portugal either side of their loss by the same score in Cardiff.

Norway and Wales still have a chance of finishing second behind Portugal, but they are also battling each other to avoid potential relegation from the Nations League's top tier.

"It's like a boxing game, going head-to-head, fist-to-fist," said Solbakken.

"I think Wales has always been a very attacking team under Bellamy. They've had great progress with the ball.

"I think it suits the team with the offensive players they have, the speed on the wings and Harry Wilson back. And [Lewis] Koumas getting more minutes for Liverpool, so I think that suits them.

"I'm not surprised that they will go all in but it's our home game so obviously I think they will also have their struggles with us. Let's see."

Wales head coach Bellamy and winger Daniel James, who scored their first goal in Cardiff last month, have said they are mindful of Norway's desire to exact revenge.

Asked if that was an incentive for his side, Solbakken said: "I think both teams need to win the game, so you can call it revenge or whatever.

"I think we were very passive in the first half against Wales. We had no intensity in our play. We were decent with the ball, but we were crap without the ball.

"Overall, they deserved to lead by half-time and then there was our red card one minute into the second half.

"I think the first half was our worst performance in two years, we have to be honest about that.

"It's two aims for us now in this football year. That is to at least be going for the third place first, and that we can do tomorrow. It's a crucial game."

articles.title: Portugal vs Denmark: UEFA Nations League – predictions, how to watch, teams
articles.summary: Playing their first game since Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, two-time champions Portugal face Denmark at home.
articles.body:
Who : Portugal vs Denmark What : UEFA Nations League, Group A4 Where : Braga Municipal Stadium, Braga, Portugal When : Saturday, November 14, at 7:45pm (19:45 GMT). How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:45 GMT before our live text commentary stream

A new chapter in Portuguese football starts on Saturday, as the national team moves on from the departure of their record scorer and longstanding captain, Cristiano Ronaldo.

Ronaldo ended his 23-year association with the Selecao last week, announcing his retirement in a lengthy video on social media, weeks after a public rift with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus.

The 41-year-old, a polarising football icon who wore the much-adored No 7 shirt for his country, said it was now time to “pass it on to the future”.

Playing their first game without their biggest star, Portugal face Denmark in Saturday’s home fixture, having already confirmed their spot in the quarterfinals.

With three goals each, forwards Goncalo Ramos and Joao Felix have orchestrated Portugal’s attacking play in Ronaldo’s absence, while Denmark’s charge has been led by Rasmus Hojlund, who has netted three of his team’s seven goals so far.

Two-time holders Portugal will be confirmed as group winners if they avoid defeat against Denmark, who are second in the standings.

The Danes have a bit more complicated path to secure their spot in the last eight on Saturday – they need to win against Portugal and hope that neighbours Norway do not beat third-placed Wales in a clash of the bottom two.

How have Portugal played in the Nations League?

Portugal have a perfect record in the competition, with four wins out of four.

They began their title defence with a 1-0 home win over Wales before beating Norway 2-1 , a game in which Ronaldo was an unused substitute.

Shortly afterwards, Ronaldo stormed out of the national camp , but his absence did not trouble the team as they thrashed Denmark 4-2 in another away game before winning 2-1 at home against Norway to reach the quarterfinals.

How have Denmark played in the Nations League?

Denmark have won two games and lost two.

Their campaign started with a 3-2 loss in Norway, but they bounced back with a 2-0 home victory against Wales.

The third match saw them fall 4-2 at home to Portugal before they beat Wales 1-0 away.

What happened when Portugal and Denmark last met?

Goals from Joao Cancelo, Goncalo Ramos, Vitinha and Felix gave Portugal a 4-2 win over Denmark on October 1.

Mikkel Damsgaard and Rasmus Hojlund scored for the hosts in that game at Copenhagen.

Opta’s supercomputer has given Portugal a 59.4 percent probability of victory, while Denmark’s odds stand at 19.4 percent.

There is a 21.2 percent chance the game ends in a draw.

articles.title: El cambio detrás del mejor Baena de su carrera
articles.standfirst: Tras intervenir en un gol del Atlético o España con más frecuencia de lo que hizo en su mejor curso en el Villarreal (cada 1,75 partidos, frente a 2,03), el secreto está en su cuerpo y mente
articles.summary: Tras intervenir en un gol del Atlético o España con más frecuencia de lo que hizo en su mejor curso en el Villarreal (cada 1,75 partidos, frente a 2,03), el secreto está en su cuerpo y mente
articles.body: Tras el último gol de Baena a la República Checa, su hoja de servicios en este curso se eleva a siete dianas y cinco asistencias en los 21 partidos disputados con el Atlético y la selección española. Unos números que arrojan una participación en la perforación del marco rival cada 1,75 apariciones, frecuencia aún mayor (2,03) que la de la temporada 23-24 en la que había establecido su techo con ocho tantos y 19 pases decisivos en 55 citas con el Villarreal. El talento no ha cambiado, pero sí el cuerpo y la mente que permiten explicar la eclosión en la mejor versión jamás vista del 10 rojiblanco. Precisamente por sus tres últimas campañas como amarillo en las que empezó a labrarse un hueco en la selección antes de levantar la Eurocopa y colgarse la medalla de oro en los Juegos Olímpicos, el estreno de Baena como rojiblanco acabó con una clara sensación de desilusión. Cierto es que sufrió una apendicitis y dos lesiones musculares en los primeros meses que le lastraron notablemente, pero tanto sus cifras como su peso en el equipo no fueron ni mucho menos las esperadas. Cabe recordar que en la campaña 22-23 firmaría 13 goles y siete asistencias en 59 encuentros (Eurocopa sub 21 conquistada incluida) y en la 24-25 marcaría ocho y repartiría diez en 38 apariciones, revelando que participaba en un tanto cada 2,95 y 2,11 partidos. Nada que ver con sus discretos números en sus primeras citas con el Atlético: tres dianas, cuatro pases de la muerte, una intervención decisiva cada 8,57 presencias. Sin embargo, sólo se trataba del inicio de un proceso que ha tornado en la construcción del mejor Baena de su carrera. Del mismo modo que las estadísticas hablan por sí solas, los parámetros físicos también han cambiado por completo. Es por ahí, de hecho, por donde los que viven el día a día junto a Baena explican su salto de calidad en el juego. Su técnica y su creatividad es la misma, pero no así el cuerpo ni la mente que le permiten ahora explotar su talento. En este sentido, lejos de cuestionar su primer año como rojiblanco, en el Atlético consideran que ha resultado clave para que Baena lograra unas adaptaciones fisiológicas y musculares en su cuerpo que le convierten en un jugador totalmente distinto, más preparado para la exigencia de competir prácticamente cada tres días al más alto nivel. Al mismo tiempo, también se destaca su adaptación a un modelo de juego tan marcado como el del Atlético que nada tiene que ver con el que acostumbraba en el Villarreal o al que impera en la selección. Así, los esfuerzos defensivos no son los mismos, ni la intensidad, ni las responsabilidades sin balón. De ahí que poco tengan que ver sus funciones ni aunque en los tres casos parta desde el costado izquierdo. De hecho, sus métricas físicas pueden llegar a ser menores disputando un partido completo con España que en uno siendo sustituido como rojiblanco. Valga como ejemplo también la comparación entre los kilómetros que recorren Lamine y Giuliano pese a que ambos sean extremos. Por último, tampoco se deja de lado el impacto anímico que ha tenido el Mundial para Baena. Una experiencia que ha acabado de elevar su autoestima y que ha potenciado su personalidad y su capacidad de liderazgo. En este sentido, su caso es una clara representación de la delgada línea que puede tener el factor mental, pues quizás de haber estado Nico Williams en plenitud su rol en la conquista de la selección no habría sido el mismo. Sin embargo, su habilidad para estar preparado y aprovechar el momento ha servido para dispararle también en el plano psicológico.

articles.title: Los dos hombres de Mourinho en la sombra que explican el milagro
articles.standfirst: António Dias y Sandro Carriço están detrás de una nueva estructura de preparación física y control de cargas que ha permitido al Madrid cambiar su tendencia con las lesiones
articles.summary: António Dias y Sandro Carriço están detrás de una nueva estructura de preparación física y control de cargas que ha permitido al Madrid cambiar su tendencia con las lesiones
articles.body: "¿Queréis una historia? Yo os la busco". José Mourinho lanzó el reto en una rueda de prensa de octubre. Y la historia estaba en Valdebebas. Por primera vez en al menos diez años, el Real Madrid había llegado a mediados de octubre sin que ningún futbolista se hubiera perdido un partido por una lesión sufrida durante la temporada. Los jugadores que seguían en la enfermería arrastraban problemas del curso anterior. Una situación muy distinta a la de las últimas campañas, en las que las bajas se habían convertido en una constante. La disponibilidad de la plantilla había sido uno de los grandes condicionantes del equipo. Ahora, el escenario es otro. No significa que el Madrid haya dejado de tener futbolistas lesionados ni que esté a salvo de nuevos contratiempos (Mourinho recordó que también interviene la suerte, especialmente en las lesiones traumáticas), pero sí que el equipo ha conseguido reducir de forma notable los problemas físicos que aparecen durante la competición. La temporada pasada, a estas alturas, el Madrid llevaba ya 17 lesiones. En la actual, siete... de las cuales tres se han producido con las selecciones y la de Asencio que arrastra de la temporada pasada. Tan sólo una lesión muscular: Valverde, que estuvo diez días de baja. Detrás de ese cambio hay una estructura de trabajo en la que el entrenador ha querido intervenir desde su llegada. Dos nombres destacan por encima del resto: António Dias y Sandro Carriço. Son dos hombres de su confianza, incorporados desde su etapa en Portugal, que trabajan desde perfiles distintos y complementarios. Dias está al frente de la preparación física; Carriço aporta su especialización en fisiología y ciencias del deporte. Junto a ellos siguen Antonio Pintus y el departamento médico, dentro de un engranaje que Mourinho ha definido como un 'plan global'. La trayectoria de António Dias tiene un comienzo poco habitual para alguien que hoy dirige buena parte del trabajo físico del Real Madrid. Portugués, nacido en 1982 y licenciado en Ciencias de la Actividad Física y el Deporte, empezó su camino en el Oporto como traductor. Una coincidencia durante una estancia Erasmus en Italia le abrió la puerta del club. Su labor inicial duró apenas un mes: sus conocimientos le llevaron pronto a colaborar también en la recuperación de los jugadores y, más adelante, a participar directamente en los entrenamientos. Su carrera quedó ligada durante años a la de Nuno Espírito Santo, con quien trabajó en Rio Ave, Valencia, Oporto, Wolverhampton, Nottingham Forest, Al-Ittihad y Tottenham. Mourinho se fijó en él en 2025 y lo incorporó a su proyecto. Desde entonces, ambos han coincidido en Fenerbahce, Benfica y Real Madrid. Es uno de los hombres de máxima confianza del entrenador y, aunque Pintus continúa en el club, Dias ha asumido un papel protagonista en la preparación física del equipo. Su método combina el trabajo de fuerza en el gimnasio con su aplicación inmediata al fútbol. No se trataba de acumular trabajo físico sin más, sino de trasladar esa fuerza a los gestos y esfuerzos que exige un partido. En Valdebebas hablan maravillas de su exigencia y su meticulosidad, siempre acompañadas de buen carácter y una sonrisa. Los que le conocen aseguran que es una persona muy metódica y organizada, con un perfil muy tranquilo y discreto. No le gusta ser protagonista. Los jugadores valoran la tranquilidad y la confianza que les transmite. También procura trabajar el aspecto mental de los jugadores, apelando a su capacidad de integración y colaboración dentro del grupo. Algo que le ha permitido caer de pie nada más llegar al Madrid. Sandro Carriço llegó al Real Madrid después de trece años en el Benfica. Había trabajado primero con los equipos de formación y después con el primer equipo, donde coincidió con Mourinho durante la etapa del técnico en Lisboa. Su incorporación respondió a una necesidad detectada por el entrenador y por el propio Dias: reforzar el área de fisiología con un especialista de confianza. Su función se sitúa en un plano distinto al de la preparación física más visible. Como especialista en ciencias del deporte, su trabajo se centra en estudiar cómo responde el organismo de cada futbolista al ejercicio y a la acumulación de esfuerzos. La monitorización de las cargas, la fatiga, el descanso y la recuperación permiten ajustar el trabajo a las necesidades individuales y detectar señales que puedan anticipar un problema físico. En este aspecto su trabajo ha sido clave para lograr esta racha tan positiva. No es una labor que se aprecie desde la grada, pero sí una parte importante de la planificación diaria. La información que se obtiene sobre el estado de los jugadores ayuda a decidir cuánto exigir, cuándo recuperar y cuándo conviene modificar una sesión. Otro perfil que ha encajado muy bien en Valdebebas: "Es una persona con buen carácter, a los jugadores les encanta bromear con él", aseguran. Gimnasio, prevención, seguimiento individual y comunicación entre los distintos departamentos forman parte de una rutina que no siempre trasciende, pero que condiciona la disponibilidad de la plantilla.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: New Man Utd head coach in tears as he labels leaving USMNT 'toughest decision of career'
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has said leaving the United States to join Man Utd was the 'toughest decision of his career'; Pochettino will begin in his new role after he has led the USMNT in their two games against Haiti; the former Spurs boss has agreed a deal at Old Trafford until 2029
articles.body:
Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup.

The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference before his penultimate game, Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision.

"In some part, this is a very sad decision. In another part, we are professionals. This is the next step to try and make your dreams come true," the former Spurs and Chelsea boss said.

"It all happened so quickly. By Sunday afternoon there was contact. You always were transparent and always tried to build something together. We learned a lot from you all, this amazing country and you amazing people. This is one of the most difficult decisions of my career. Thank you so much."

Pochettino last held a club role in Europe during his one-season stint at Chelsea, which came to an end in 2024. When asked why he had opted to leave his post to return to the Premier League, Pochettino didn't hide the fact that taking the Old Trafford hot seat was a once in a lifetime opportunity.

"It's obvious," Pochettino added. "They [US Soccer Federation] know that not many opportunities can happen in your career like a side the size of Manchester United.

"When that arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Pochettino explains why he is staying for two more games

Pochettino will start life at Carrington following the international break, and will have three training sessions with the players before the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

The new head coach admitted that he would have started sooner if asked to, but explained why he wanted to see out the remainder of this camp.

"I am a professional person and the emotional link between us we have built in this two years is to show the commitment and respect and care and love," Pochettino said.

"Even if we take a decision which is not the best for one part, we've always been open. We have the respect of the players and staff, they understand the situation.

"Of course, if Manchester United and the federation agreed different terms, I would have respected between both. But this happened and of course, all the games are important.

"The last four games were important. We gave debuts to 13 players, before the cup I thought everyone had different ideas about it but we believe in the programme and are brave enough to go ahead. We're always optimistic and positive.

"After this camp, with four victories, we've been consistent in the same way, win or lose. We believe in the programme. It's an honour for us to be here, defend our patch and our players.

"We need to play tomorrow and the next game. We're not thinking in the future, it's about performing. We're very optimistic and it's a natural way to finish our partnership."

Emotional Poch rediscovered motivation in USA

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol :

"We've always known Mauricio Pochettino is an emotional person. He wears his heart on his sleeve. But I don't think you would normally expect a manager to break down and be so emotional in a press conference when he was leaving the USA to manage Manchester United.

"But that just tells you about the kind of guy he is because he's all about personal relationships. And obviously, he's made some very good friends in the US.

"He also said: 'We recovered our motivation here'. He was quite hurt and bruised by what happened to him at PSG and at Chelsea. It's almost like he's rediscovered his motivation by working in the US. And now he's ready to come back to the Premier League."

Carrick’s unintentional advice to Pochettino

In the wake of the announcement of Pochettino as the new head coach at Old Trafford, his predecessor Michael Carrick penned an emotional farewell off the back of his sacking on Wednesday.

Carrick took to social media to thank supporters saying, “you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way".

In his post, the former Red Devils midfielder also lent an inadvertent word of advice for his replacement, giving an insight into what life is like at the club.

“To be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means,” Carrick added.

"It's different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

"It's a football club that's unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored.”

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino in tears over 'difficult' decision to leave USA for Manchester United
articles.summary: An emotional Mauricio Pochettino broke down as he explained why he was leaving the USA to take the Manchester United job.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino says the decision to leave his role as boss of the USA national team to become Manchester United head coach was "one of the most difficult" of his career.

The Argentine was announced as Michael Carrick's successor at Old Trafford on Friday, with sources telling BBC Sport he has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract.

United paid a release clause in the region of £7.4m to extract Pochettino from his USA contract, with a further payment being made for his backroom staff.

Pochettino only signed a new four-year deal with the USA in the summer, but will depart for Manchester after leading the national team in matches against Haiti on 14 and 18 November.

The 54-year-old broke down in tears during his first news conference after his move to United was confirmed, and thanked the US Soccer Federation for its support.

"It's difficult to talk now," he said. "I'm a very emotional guy. It's a very sad decision.

"But we are professionals and we are trying to make our dreams come true."

Asked why he signed a new deal with the national side only to accept United's offer, Pochettino said the chance to manage at Old Trafford was too good to reject.

"I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United," he said. "When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Carrick was sacked on Thursday after United's worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years, which has left them languishing in 18th place in the Premier League.

Pochettino will inherit a side that have won just once in 10 league matches this season and sit just one point above bottom-placed Sunderland.

His first match in charge will be an away match against Liverpool on 22 November.

How Ferguson-inspired Pochettino can succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd

Pochettino's arrival at Old Trafford marks the end of a decade-long courtship.

Thriving during an 18-month stint at Southampton, he led the Saints to eighth place during his only full season on the south coast.

Tottenham moved quickly to appoint one of the most promising young coaches in Europe in 2014, and it was in north London that his reputation rocketed.

The club had finished in the top four just twice in the 22 years before his appointment, but Pochettino led them there four times in his five full seasons.

It was two years into his time in the capital that United first considered a move for Pochettino.

The Argentine dined with legendary former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson in Mayfair, London just weeks before Louis van Gaal was sacked as Red Devils boss.

The club ultimately decided to appoint Jose Mourinho, and Pochettino was again overlooked when the Portuguese departed in 2018, with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer impressing so much in an interim role that he was given the job more permanently.

In 2022, it was between Pochettino and Erik ten Hag for the United job but the board opted for the Dutchman, who had led Ajax to the semi-finals of the Champions League in 2019, when they were beaten by Pochettino's Tottenham.

Pochettino was interviewed by United again in 2024 following his exit from Chelsea, but the board opted instead to hire Ruben Amorim from Sporting to replace Ten Hag.

Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better

Carrick 'incredibly grateful' despite exit

Shortly after Pochettino's appointment, Carrick released a statement on social media thanking United's fans for their support during his time in charge of the club.

"Dear United fans, I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love," wrote Carrick. , external

"There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

"With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means.

In a wide-ranging post, Carrick, who signed a two-year deal with the club in May, said the club's culture and values drove him at Old Trafford.

"Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time," he wrote.

"It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored.

"This is what inspired me every single day."

The chaos that took Carrick from two-year deal to sacked within 15 games

United board unanimous about hiring Pochettino

Manchester United have made it pretty clear Mauricio Pochettino is the only coach they spoke to directly about taking over at Old Trafford.

Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte were also mentioned as possibles in the aftermath of that awful 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth three weeks ago, but evidently Pochettino emerged as the first choice.

Interestingly, United have felt it necessary to state privately any claim of a split between the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe is "categorically false" in their words.

I reported earlier this week a mechanism by which the Glazer family could take back control of the football operation from Ratcliffe.

There has been no Stock Exchange statement that has happened - there was one that Ratcliffe had been handed control by the board when he agreed to buy into United in December 2023.

There has been huge criticism by fans of the way United are being run. Sporting director Jason Wilcox is blamed by many for bad recruitment, but the budget was set higher up.

United officials are keen to stress unanimity in the hierarchy but with the club 18th in the Premier League and having sacked three managers in three seasons, none of the owners can be happy. It is one to keep an eye on.

articles.summary: Un dato importante para este partido de carácter amistoso: se permiten hasta nueve cambios, un margen amplio para repartir minutos entre una lista de
articles.body:
Última hora del España - Japón en directo:

Muy buenas tardes y bienvenidos al directo de este partido. España sub-21 se enfrente a Japón en un amistoso que se va a disputar en el Estadio Francisco de la Hera de Almendralejo (Extremadura). Un partido de preparación ya para el próximo Europeo de la categoría.

España ya sabe que estará en el Europeo sub-21. Lo selló el 6 de octubre en Can Misses, con un 7-1 a Rumanía que cerró la fase de clasificación con nueve victorias en diez partidos, 47 goles a favor y cinco en contra, según la RFEF. Pero el trabajo de David Gordo empieza ahora, y con el calendario justo: el torneo arranca el 16 de junio de 2027 en Albania y Serbia, y al seleccionador le quedan «cuatro o cinco partidos solo» para «aprovechar al máximo las ventanas».

El primero de ellos llega hoy ante un rival que también tiene prisa. Japón aterriza en Almendralejo con la generación que apunta a los Juegos de Los Ángeles 2028 y con un técnico, Tsuyoshi iwa, que quiere comprobar cuánto funciona su estilo frente a selecciones de nivel. Gordo lo resumió en la rueda de prensa de la convocatoria con una frase corta: "un pedazo de equipo".

El partido funciona así como un laboratorio. En el lado español quedan abiertas dos plazas con nombre propio, la de delantero centro y la de la medular, y en el japonés una asignatura pendiente que el equipo arrastra desde los Juegos Asiáticos: convertir en goles las ocasiones que ya sabe crear.

articles.title: Eli Manning Gives Arch Advice for Remainder of Texas Season in New Video Ahead of LSU Matchup
articles.summary: Heading into the 2026 college football season, Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning was among the betting favorites to win the Heisman Trophy. Since then, inconsistency and questionable decision-making have cast doubt on the legacy quarterback's future.
articles.body:
Heading into the 2026 college football season, Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning was among the betting favorites to win the Heisman Trophy. Since then, inconsistency and questionable decision-making have cast doubt on the legacy quarterback's future.

Manning's uncle, two-time Super Bowl champion Eli Manning, offered his nephew some advice during an appearance on SportsCenter .

"Hey, you know, it's never going to be perfect," Eli said. "That's why you play the game. It's not always going to be smooth. Every game, every series is an opportunity to learn, to get better. You've got to learn how to just kind of take the up and downs of a game.

"There's gonna be a couple of series you have a three-and-out. Hey, you're going to throw an interception, but you're also going to make some plays. And you can never let one series kind of dictate your mindset going into the next one. And I think he's done a good job overcoming those things and just bouncing back, always being present, and being able to step up late in games and make the plays that he needs to [make]. So he's still a young quarterback. He's learning each and every week. They're playing well right now, he's in a good rhythm. Hopefully he can keep that going."

Manning led the Longhorns to the No. 1 ranking after the team's first four games, but Texas plummeted down rankings and draft boards after two consecutive losses against unranked Oklahoma and Florida.

Texas has rebounded since then, and the team picked up its third straight victory on Saturday against No. 18 Missouri. Manning threw three touchdowns with no interceptions as the Longhorns improved to a 7-2 record.

"I've been proud of Arch, of how he's handled this season," Eli said. "It hasn't been totally perfect, but they've had some big wins. You get wins against Ohio State early, you get wins on the road in the SEC, it's not easy."

The Longhorns will face the No. 21 LSU Tigers on Saturday in a game that could have massive playoff implications.

articles.summary: There's a bit of clarity at the top of the College Football Playoff rankings with three weeks left in the regular season.
articles.body:
There's a bit of clarity at the top of the College Football Playoff rankings with three weeks left in the regular season.

The Georgia Bulldogs have established, for now, that they are the top-ranked team in the country.

The two remaining undefeated teams, the Utah Utes and UCLA Bruins, have inside tracks to first-round byes in the 12-team playoff field.

The Notre Dame Fighting Irish sit at No. 5 with a clear directive to win out to have a shot at the top four, and at minimum, confirm a playoff spot.

Most of the CFB Playoff drama will occur in the bottom half of the top 12 because a handful of teams have dropped from those places on a week-by-week basis.

Georgia is on the inside track to land the No. 1 overall seed in the CFB Playoff.

The Bulldogs are back at No. 1 after the Miami Hurricanes fell to Notre Dame in Week 10.

Kirby Smart's team can add a pair of ranked victories to its resume in the next two weeks against the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks.

UGA could be 5-0 against ranked foes going into the SEC Championship Game, where it would have a chance to land another Top 25 victory.

Six wins against Top 25 teams would be enough to claim the No. 1 overall seed, especially if UCLA, Utah and Notre Dame are the other three teams in the top four.

No single team has been clear above the rest in college football this season, but if UGA goes into the playoff at 12-1, it has the case to be the clear favorite to win the playoff.

The race for the at-large positions could go any which way in the next three weeks.

A week ago, the Ohio State Buckeyes, LSU Tigers and Ole Miss Rebels lost to take themselves out of at-large contention.

Any team outside the top five should not feel confident about their place in the 12-team field, especially the ninth-ranked Indiana Hoosiers, who fell five spots on their bye week because of their weak schedule.

The fight for the last two or three spots, though, could be the most fascinating competition.

The BYU Cougars or Texas Tech Red Raiders would land in the Big 12 Championship Game, which puts them at risk for another loss at the hands of No. 2 Utah.

The Kentucky Wildcats have a tough road test against the Missouri Tigers in Week 12 and the Tennessee Volunteers still have to play LSU at home on the same weekend.

Any potential losses opens the door for the Wake Forest Demon Deacons, Houston Cougars, Iowa Hawkeyes, or others further down the rankings to place themselves into the top 11.

Unpredictability has been the theme of the 2026 college football season, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see the rankings mixed up a few more times before Selection Sunday.

articles.title: Tare: ‘Milan biggest disappointment was Pulisic, choosing Allegri, Cardinale problem’
articles.summary: Milan sacked Igli Tare in May, but he has broken his silence on why he chose Max Allegri, not getting the chance to speak to owner Gerry Cardinale, and why ‘...
articles.body:
Milan sacked Igli Tare in May, but he has broken his silence on why he chose Max Allegri, not getting the chance to speak to owner Gerry Cardinale, and why 'Christian Pulisic was the biggest disappointment.'

The former Lazio chief was brought in as director of sport, a role that until his arrival had not existed at the club for a while, since the dismissal of Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara in 2023.

He did not even last a full year, as Tare was sacked along with coach Allegri, CEO Giorgio Furlani and director Geoffrey Moncada with a single, brutal press statement on May 25.

VERONA, ITALY – APRIL 19: Igli Tare, Sporting Director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Hellas Verona FC and AC Milan at Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi on April 19, 2026 in Verona, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images)

"The wound of failing to qualify for the Champions League is still deep, enormous in fact," Tare told Sky Sport Italia Calcio Unplugged.

"If I come to a club like Milan with the target of getting into the Champions League, then I don't know where I am. This is the most successful club in Italian football history, and after Real Madrid it is the most important in the world."

RedBird patron Cardinale had been an aloof figure at first, but decided after cleaning house that he would take a much more hands-on approach to running the club.

"I am disappointed that those leading the club didn't understand people needed to be given time, something that they are now doing better," added Tare.

PISA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 13: Igli Tare of AC Milan looks on during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and AC Milan at Arena Garibaldi on February 13, 2026 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)

"I'd say you need several transfer market sessions to get a team that is competitive and ready to win. At the start, there was an important responsibility, missing out on Europe altogether and losing the Coppa Italia Final did a lot of damage to morale.

"We sold players for a lot of money and signed 10 new figures, so it takes time to integrate, understand and create a united group. We had, albeit in difficult circumstances, been first or second up until the end of March and start of April. In the last 10 rounds, our mentality just collapsed due to other issues that I don't want to get into, but they did have an effect.

"I admit we too deserve some of the blame, because Max and I should've paid more attention to certain dynamics, be more present with the squad to get the season over the line."

UDINE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Igli Tare, Sporting director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and AC Milan at Stadio Friuli on September 20, 2025 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

When Tare was brought in, it was meant to be as a director of sport, but he insists he never had a direct line to the man with the purse strings.

"I remember when we were in negotiations for Ardon Jashari, he called and wanted to understand what was happening. He said 'if you need to spend a little more, just let me know, and I'm ready.' However, I never got the chance to speak with him directly again, because there were people above me I didn't want to over-ride.

"It would've been helpful to everyone, not just me, if we'd been able to discuss it directly. I think this is a new experience for Cardinale, he is used to other sports in America, but now he has taken on the responsibility at Milan.

"I would've preferred to have that presence when I was still at Milan, as it would've been very useful, but better late than never for the good of the club. I think the good of Milan is top of his priorities too."

MILAN, ITALY – APRIL 26: Luka Modric of AC Milan is consoled by Massimiliano Allegri, Head Coach of AC Milan, as he is assisted off by medical staff after going down injured during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Juventus FC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on April 26, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Among the roles tasked to Tare was the choice of a new coach, and he plumped for Allegri.

"I was thinking of the experience he brought at that time. When I arrived, the only thing I was asked was to hire an Italian coach, not a foreign one," revealed Tare.

"I had a few ideas for foreign coaches, but the experience with Sergio Conceicao and Paulo Fonseca evidently wasn't what they were after. Allegri won a lot as a coach, Milan is special to him, he won the Scudetto there first, so of course he was sad at the way it ended.

"He is not alone, Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Alessandro Nesta had great experiences elsewhere too, but Milan stands out for them, and I can confirm it's true."

SALZBURG, AUSTRIA – OCTOBER 15: Luka Modric of AC Milan looks on before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Salzburg and AC Milan at Stadion Salzburg on October 15, 2026 in Salzburg, Austria. (Photo by Jasmin Walter/Getty Images)

This is also a legendary club abroad, and it is what prompted the arrival of Ballon d'Or winner Luka Modric as a free agent after the experience at Real Madrid.

"I had the sensation this squad lacked leadership. The idea along with Modric was to sign Granit Xhaka, who at the time was the captain of Bayer Leverkusen, to guide the others. Luka is more silent in his attitude on the pitch."

There was an intriguing comment from Tare that suggested more tension behind the scenes with some players.

"The biggest disappointment was Pulisic, I expected more from him in terms of responsibility and leadership. He's a great player, but some things happened that I had never experienced in my career. Pulisic didn't score a goal for six months. Santiago Gimenez didn't score either.

"I guess these things happen in football, but when you have a drought that long, it ends up affecting the whole team's performance."

articles.title: Longtime NFL QB and former NC State QB Philip Rivers named the Wolfpack's new head coach
articles.summary: Rivers had been negotiating with NC State since at least Sunday.
articles.body:
Philip Rivers is now officially NC State's new head football coach.

The school announced Friday that it had hired the former Wolfpack QB to take over at the end of the season. NC State fired Dave Doeren after a 3-4 start to the 2026 season that included a disastrous loss to Vanderbilt.

"Philip Rivers is one of one and the right person to lead NC State Football into its next era," athletic director Boo Corrigan said in a statement. "His accomplishments as a player at the collegiate and professional levels speak for themselves. But throughout this search process, what stood out to me most was his exceptional leadership ability, his character, the way he connects with people and his vision for this program. He is someone who is deeply respected and beloved by Wolfpack Nation, and I couldn't be more proud that he will be the one leading our football program."

Rivers, 44, doesn't have any collegiate coaching experience and is currently the head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama. His son, Gunner Rivers, is St. Michael's QB. Gunner Rivers is a longtime NC State commit and a four-star prospect in the class of 2027.

NC State is 4-5 after a loss to Duke in Week 10. The Wolfpack need to win two of their final three games under interim coach Todd Goebbel to make a bowl game.

Doeren had been NC State's coach since 2013 and led the school to eight seasons of eight or more wins. The Wolfpack were 8-5 in 2025 but lost back-to-back games to Wake Forest and Stanford before Doeren was fired. In Week 3, QB CJ Bailey fumbled in the NC State end zone while trying to run out the clock to secure a victory. Vanderbilt recovered the ball and won 35-31.

Rivers was a four-year QB at NC State from 2000 to 2003 before he was the No. 4 pick in the 2004 NFL Draft. He was drafted by the Giants and then traded to the Chargers, as Eli Manning didn't want to play for San Diego.

Before he was drafted, Rivers was the 2003 ACC player of the year. He finished seventh in Heisman voting that season. He will reportedly make $3.25 million per season on a five-year deal.

"I am humbled and honored to be the next head football coach at NC State University," Rivers said in the school's release. "In many ways, I feel like I'm coming home. This is where it all began for me as an 18-year-old kid from Alabama, and now to return to this great place as head coach is beyond words. "I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games and I will give it everything I have as the coach. There's no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we're not scared of hard. I look forward to getting after it every single day with an unbelievable coaching staff and a group of players who are dedicated to relentlessly pursuing victory."

He was then out of the league for four seasons before the Colts signed him near the end of the 2025 season because of Daniel Jones' Achilles injury. Rivers started three games as the Colts attempted to make the playoffs, but Indianapolis lost all three and missed the postseason.

articles.title: Ronaldinho aterriza en Italia para preparar su regreso de este domingo
articles.standfirst: Podría tener minutos con el Ravenna en el derbi frente al Forli
articles.summary: Podría tener minutos con el Ravenna en el derbi frente al Forli
articles.body: El exfutbolista brasileño Ronaldinho Gaúcho llegó este viernes a Italia para preparar su regreso a los terrenos de juego con el Ravena, equipo de la Serie C italiana, con el que podría disputar el próximo domingo el derbi frente al Forli. El brasileño, de 46 años, aterrizó en el aeropuerto de Forlì (norte de Italia), donde fue recibido por el presidente del club, Ignazio Cipriani, con quien mantiene una buena relación. El entrenador del conjunto italiano, Andrea Mandorlini, avanzó que el exinternacional brasileño podría disputar alrededor de media hora en el encuentro, aunque todavía no ha confirmado en qué posición jugará y si saldrá desde el once inicial o desde el banquillo. Ronaldinho tiene previsto realizar este sábado su primer entrenamiento con sus nuevos compañeros, después de una sesión individual programada para este viernes, según adelantaron medios locales. El encuentro supondría el regreso de Ronaldinho a la competición oficial, once años después de disputar su último partido profesional, tras cerrar su etapa en el Fluminense en 2015. Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, conocido como Ronaldinho, fue uno de los grandes referentes del fútbol brasileño y mundial. Se proclamó campeón del mundo con Brasil en 2002, conquistó el Balón de Oro en 2005 y fue elegido en dos ocasiones mejor jugador del mundo por la FIFA. Durante su carrera militó en clubes como Gremio, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona y Milan, además de Flamengo, Atlético Mineiro, Querétaro y Fluminense. Su etapa más brillante llegó en el Barcelona, con el que ganó dos ligas españolas y una Liga de Campeones. Su fútbol le convirtió en uno de los jugadores más reconocidos de su generación.
